data.title: How to Build a Smartwatch: Picking a Chip
data.author: rcarmo
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何选择芯片来制作智能手表，重点选择了SiFli公司的SF32LB52J芯片，该芯片具备开源SDK。作者计划发布一系列关于制作智能手表的帖子，包括选择芯片、硬件和软件等方面。智能手表由手表硬件、软件和移动 companion app 三大组件构成。选择微控制器和蓝牙芯片以及显示屏是设计中的主要挑战。文章还回顾了Pebble时代使用STM32F2芯片的经历，强调选择合适芯片对于平衡软件兼容性、功耗和成本至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PebbleOS及相关开源硬件和软件在智能手表领域的应用与发展

不同观点：
• [rjmunro] 提到除了 PebbleOS 之外，还有 Espruino（一个用于微控制器的小型 JavaScript 实现），并提供了相关链接和示例，如 Bangle.js 和 Fallout Pip-Boy，指出其易于实时修改和扩展。
• [rgoulter] 对所谓的“开源”提出了质疑，指出虽然 SDK 是开源的，但 BLE 代码是以二进制形式提供的，无法查看源码，认为这在描述上存在误导性。
• [wkat4242] 认为 Pebble 和 rePebble 虽然电池寿命长，但在功能上不如现代智能手表，如缺少 NFC 支付、双频 GPS 跟踪和 4G LTE 连接等功能，因此不愿为了长续航放弃现代智能手表的强大功能。
• [mrheosuper] 讨论了芯片设计的选择，指出没有采用双芯片设计（一个用于主应用，一个用于 BLE）可能是因为高功耗 MCU 通常不具备 RF 功能。
• [alin23] 表达了对开源低功耗芯片的兴趣，但个人更倾向于一种带震动通知功能的“哑巴表”，并描述了自己对小米手环的体验和当前寻找小型蓝牙芯片的需求。

补充讨论：
• [zoobab] 分享了自己对廉价中国 Freqchip  SoC 的研究，并提供了相关 GitHub 链接，指出可以通过 AliExpress 以极低价格购买搭载此芯片的智能手表。
• [outadoc] 对文章的排版提出了意见，认为在2025年仍然使用左对齐的博客格式不够现代化，阅读体验不佳。
• [amelius] 对软件兼容性被视为最困难的约束提出了异议，认为这是最容易解决的问题，并建议将其放在待解决问题列表的末尾。
• [Shalomboy] 对文章中提到的 nimBLE 蓝牙栈表示赞赏，认为这将为核心设备带来有趣的机会。
• [ENadyr] 对文章内容表示赞赏，并开玩笑说希望在 YC 期间能有这些信息来帮助决策。
• [aswanson] 简单表达了对该产品功能集和价格的赞赏。

争议焦点：
• 开源的定义和透明度：[rgoulter] 对 BLE 代码以二进制形式提供表示不满，认为这与“开源”的描述不符。
• 功能与续航的取舍：[wkat4242] 强调现代智能手表的功能重要性，而 [alin23] 则更倾向于简单的震动通知功能，反映出不同用户对智能手表的需求差异。

← Back to Home
How To Build A Smartwatch: Picking A Chip
[
2025-05-12
]
Full video of this post is up on my podcast on
YouTube
! Subscribe on
PocketCasts
,
Spotify
, or
Apple Podcasts
.
TLDR:
We've selected a chip for Core Time 2 - SF32LB52J. It’s from a company called SiFli, and features an open source SDK.
I’m writing a series of posts on how to make a smartwatch
Covering how to pick a chip (today), other hardware and software stuff (later)
I hope others will use PebbleOS to build interesting new smartwatches and other devices!
This is the first in a series of posts around the steps you need to take in order to build a smartwatch. I want to show that it's not actually that hard to make a decent one in 2025! Hopefully the work that we're doing to make these
new watches
will help other folks to build some as well.
Smartwatches are not and should not be ‘one-size fits all’ devices. I really hope that the open sourcing of PebbleOS might spark someone’s imagination and enable them to build a smartwatch that fits their needs perfectly!
A smartwatch is a system made up of three main components:
Watch hardware (this is the actual watch itself)
Watch software (usually referred to as the firmware or operating system)
Mobile companion app (iOS and Android app that sends notifications, downloads watchfaces etc)
As I've mentioned before, designing a consumer electronics product like a smartwatch is an exercise in constraint maximization. You need to identify a target experience goal (”I want a smartwatch with an always-on daylight readable display that lasts for 30 days”), then break that down into features/specifications (”e-paper display”, “Bluetooth LE”, “water resistant”, “$150 retail price”) and then create a design with hardware and software components (”Sharp Memory LCD”, “150mAh lipoly battery”, “FreeRTOS” etc) that meet your specifications and fulfill your goal.
After almost 20 years of building products, this process comes naturally to me - sometimes unprompted! I can look at any product and picture the exploded view, estimate manufacturing costs, and imagine how its software subsystems fit together. It’s a blessing and a curse!
You can break down watch hardware into five key systems:
Microcontroller chip (usually includes Bluetooth radio)
Display
Sensors and outputs (tac switches, touch, mics, accelerometer, speakers)
Other electronic components (chips, passive components, printed circuit board, battery)
Mechanical structure (watch case, glass, buttons, strap, charge cable)
Picking components for the latter 3 systems is actually quite straight forward these days. There are lots of good options available at various price points for sensors, batteries, straps, watch cases, mics, etc. Constraint maximization is relatively easy for these, I’ll wrap all these up into one blog post later.
The two most challenging component decisions that need to be made when designing a smartwatch are selecting:
a microcontroller and Bluetooth radio (this post)
a display (future post)
The backstory
During the first Pebble era, we used STM32F2 microcontrollers (MCU). Why? Because over beers on one Friday evening in 2011 at the
Hacker Dojo
a friend of mine, Hugo Fiennes, would NOT stop raving about this relatively new MCU. At the time, I was working on
inPulse
which used an LPC2103 (8K of RAM!) - he rightly thought that we were in desperate need of an upgrade.
Honestly, this is 100% typical for me. I think that all the major chip selections I’ve made have come from friends raving about a particular chip. Yes, I have a delightfully eccentric set of friends 😂 Thank you Trammell Hudson, TL Lim from Pine64, Peter Barrett and many others for your chats over the years.
An MCU is the heart of the smartwatch. Think of an MCU as a miniature computer - it contains a CPU, RAM, (usually) flash storage, i/o peripherals and sometimes radios, all within a single tiny integrated circuit.
You can the specs of the MCUs we used before on this
helpful table
- 64-144MHz, 128-256KB RAM. During this era, MCUs didn’t have integrated BT radios, so we used additional chips like TI CC2564 (that model is forever etched in my brain for some reason, probably the pain of finding a decent BT stack to use with it).
Why is picking the right MCU so important?
Getting back to constraint maximization, the MCU sits at the focal point of the most constrained governing ‘equations’ - software compatibility, power consumption and cost.
The most interesting and difficult constraint is actually software compatibility.
E
mbedded software is much more fragmented and requirement-specific than computer operating system software. Because computers are not very hard drive space constrained, kernels can be optimized for broader compatibility - Linux contains over 17,000 device drivers. PebbleOS was effectively hardcoded to support MCUs from only one company (STM). Switching to a different brand required writing new peripheral (i2c, SPI, DMA, etc) drivers, adopting a different SDK a

data.title: Show HN: Lumier – Run macOS VMs in a Docker
data.author: GreenGames
data.article_summary: 这篇文章（基于提供的内容推测）主要介绍了一个名为 "trycua/cua" 的开源项目。项目托管在代码托管平台上，用户必须登录才能更改通知设置。文章提到该项目的受欢迎程度，显示有254次代码复刻（Fork）和6.3k个星标（Star），表明其在开发者社区中具有较高的关注度和使用率。文章还涉及项目的通知设置及相关操作指引。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lumier或类似工具在macOS上运行虚拟机的技术细节及其实际应用

不同观点：
• [mynegation] 认为Lumier并非在Docker中运行虚拟机，而是通过Apple的虚拟化框架（Virtualization Framework）在macOS主机上运行虚拟机，Docker仅用于管理界面。
• [nottorp] 质疑在macOS主机上运行Linux虚拟机以快速启动macOS虚拟机的必要性，特别是在考虑Apple硬件的高价格时。
• [kristianp] 讨论了如果macOS具有namespaces和cgroups，是否会更适合此类使用场景，并指出当前命令中可能丢失的符号。
• [JayDustheadz] 关心Lumier是否能在Apple Silicon主机上运行macOS Big Sur，并询问是否能通过该虚拟机在App Store安装应用。
• [h4ck_th3_pl4n3t] 强调这并非真正的"在Docker中运行macOS虚拟机"，而是在Docker中运行Debian noVNC客户端，连接到macOS主机系统的虚拟机，认为这与传统的Docker虚拟机不同。

补充讨论：
• [roundup] 询问Lumier是否支持在虚拟机中禁用系统完整性保护（SIP）。
• [handfuloflight] 探讨是否可以在AWS EC2的Mac实例中启动虚拟机。
• [helpfulContrib] 提到已经使用UTM实现类似功能，并询问Lumier与之相比有何优势。
• [kelsey98765431] 担心Docker容器访问主机系统以启动Apple虚拟机的安全性问题。
• [OsrsNeedsf2P] 询问如何在Linux主机上运行Mac虚拟机，稍微偏离了讨论的核心主题。
• [cyberax] 关注是否可以通过此方法运行XCode并进行应用构建。

争议焦点：
• 该技术方案是否真正实现了"在Docker中运行macOS虚拟机"（[h4ck_th3_pl4n3t]的观点），还是仅仅利用Docker管理虚拟机界面。
• 在macOS主机上运行虚拟机的必要性和成本效益（[nottorp]的观点）。
• Docker容器访问主机系统以启动虚拟机的安全性（[kelsey98765431]的担忧）。

data.title: Launch HN: Jazzberry (YC X25) – AI agent for finding bugs
data.author: MarcoDewey
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Jazzberry工具的实用性、功能范围、技术实现和与其他工具的比较。

不同观点：
• [lacker] 认为工具需要在个人项目上试用，不愿意直接在专业项目中使用。他希望工具能扫描代码仓库并报告问题，以便在处理实际 pull requests 前进行测试。
• [jdefr89] 指出当前类似工具普遍存在误报问题，且难以发现高严重性/可利用的漏洞。不过，他认可LLMs在逆向工程二进制文件方面的价值，如Binary Ninja的插件在节省时间方面表现出色。
• [rylanu] 担心Jazzberry在大团队、monorepos和每日多个PR的情况下是否能有效扩展，特别是资源消耗和速度问题。
• [sublinear] 提出GitLab已有类似功能，并附上链接，暗示需要比较两者的优劣。
• [sorokod] 关心Jazzberry在自身代码上的表现，询问其自测结果。
• [AIorNot] 询问工具是否能检测前端问题，如导航错误或React网站的运行时错误。
• [ArnavAgrawal03] 赞赏工具以表格形式展示问题，并询问工具是针对整个代码库还是特定PR，以及是否使用了小型微调模型以提高速度。
• [bluelightning2k] 对演示视频选择测试CLI表示疑问，质疑这是否是工具的主要用例。
• [RainyDayTmrw] 希望看到更多“真实问题”的示例输出，以便更好地理解工具效果。
• [decodingchris] 对工具使用microVM（可能是Firecracker）表示兴趣，并询问是否遇到相关问题。
• [bigyabai] 认为动态测试在沙盒中进行是资源浪费，因为静态linter能在更短时间内完成类似任务，并指出成本问题。
• [bananapub] 质疑工具的价值，询问测试案例数量、评分机制以及如何防止模型训练过程中随机变化对产品造成影响。

补充讨论：
• 工具的扩展性和资源消耗问题在多个评论中被提及，尤其是对大团队和monorepos的适用性。
• 关于工具能否检测前端问题以及其在自身代码上的表现也是用户关心的重点。
• 多个评论提到与其他工具（如GitLab类似功能和Binary Ninja插件）的比较，突显了竞争和差异化的重要性。
• 成本和效率问题也被认为是影响工具采用的关键因素。

43990515.article_content:
Why Is Geographic Mobility Declining?
By
Urvi Neelakantan
,
John Bailey Jones
and
Yue Li
Economic Brief
May 2025, No. 25-19
Key Takeaways
In the U.S., people of all ages are moving less than they did 30 years ago. In this article, we describe some of the leading economic explanations for this decline in geographic mobility.
One set of explanations focuses on long-term trends such as population aging and expanding earnings opportunities for women.
Another set of explanations focuses on changes in the geographic distribution of earnings, urban amenities and housing prices.
From covered wagons to rental vans, moving has been an iconic feature of American life. In the past 30 years, however, moving rates have fallen dramatically. In this article, we describe leading economic explanations for the ongoing decline in mobility.
Figure 1 shows a steady decline in interstate migration rates between 1996 and 2024 across all age groups.
1
The figure also shows that moving rates are consistently higher for younger adults (25-34) than for older age groups and that mobility has declined within every age group. Thus, the overall decline in the mobility rate (age 25+) is due to a combination of population aging and mobility falling within every age group.
Enlarge
Some of the explanations for the decline in mobility involve long-term trends — such as population aging or increased earnings opportunities for women — that make moving costlier. Others appeal to changes in the geographic distribution of earnings, urban amenities and housing prices, all of which make moving less rewarding.
An Economic Framework
The explanations we discuss below fit into a widely used economic framework. Most economic models of migration focus on one or more of the following factors:
2
Employment
Earnings
Amenities (such as weather, shopping and dining)
Proximity to family and friends
Housing prices
These models begin with the assumption that individuals and families migrate when the expected benefits of living in new locations (net of moving costs) exceed the expected benefits of remaining in their current locations. They characterize individuals and locations as multidimensional: Individuals may prefer — or have skills better suited to — some jobs rather than others, and employers may offer higher wages for those jobs in one area than in another. People may also differ in the amenities they prefer, while locations may differ in the amenities they offer. These decisions drive migration flows across areas, with wages and/or housing prices mediating the flows.
Demographic Trends in Employment and Earnings
Men and Women
Figure 2 shows that the fraction of women working full time rose from 57 percent in 1996 to 61 percent in 2024, while the share of men working full time fell from 84 percent to 80 percent.
Enlarge
As Figure 3 shows, over the same period, the ratio of women's earnings to men's earnings among those working full time grew by 23 percentage points.
Enlarge
As the earnings and full-time employment rates of women approach those of men, we should expect geographic mobility to fall for a few reasons. First, dual-earner couples with similar incomes would become more common and, as shown in a 2018 working paper, couples with
similar earnings are less likely to relocate
than those with unequal earnings.
3
The paper further estimated that falling wage differences between sexes accounted for over one-third of the drop in family mobility between 1981 and 2012.
Unemployment insurance appears to mitigate this channel. A 2024 working paper estimated that providing unemployment insurance for the trailing spouse — the spouse who gives up a job to accommodate his or her partner's career move —
increased the probability that a household moves
more than 100 miles by 2.7 percentage points.
4
The convergence of earnings and employment between men and women may also increase the need for child care. This in turn could affect geographic mobility by encouraging individuals or couples with children to locate near relatives who can help with child care. For example, a 2024 working paper found that women living within 25 miles of their parents experienced a substantially smaller drop in earnings after having children than those living further away.
5
Our own analysis of the data is consistent with the above-described forces being at play. We run regressions to examine the predictors of moving across states for people aged 35-54. Table 1 reports the results.

data.title: Working on complex systems: What I learned working at Google
data.author: 0xKelsey
data.article_summary:
《The Coder Cafe：处理复杂系统》一文由Teiva Harsanyi撰写，讨论了复杂系统的概念以及在Google工作期间获得的见解。文章首先区分了“复杂问题”和“繁杂问题”：繁杂问题虽复杂但可预测并有结构化解决方案，而复杂问题则需要适应性和新颖的解决方案。例如，优化打车软件中的司机-乘客匹配属于繁杂问题，而Google的大规模机器学习基础设施则涉及真正的复杂问题。

文章进一步描述了复杂系统的五大特征：
1. **涌现行为**：系统整体行为无法通过单独分析其组成部分预测。
2. **延迟后果**：行动的后果可能不会立即显现，而是延迟出现。
3. **局部与全局优化**：优化某一部分不一定改善整体，有时甚至适得其反。
4. **滞后效应**：系统过去的状态继续影响其行为。

理解这些特征有助于识别和处理复杂系统，避免用解决繁杂问题的方法处理复杂问题，从而更有效地应对挑战。

主要讨论点：谷歌及复杂系统开发的经验与复杂性理解

不同观点：
• gilbetron认为，虽然谷歌的系统规模和复杂性很大，但谷歌的开发人员通常依赖复杂的工具来处理这些系统。他们所做的更改可能相对简单，但由于系统规模巨大，这些更改会影响大量用户。他指出，谷歌员工的经历独特，但通常与外界的预期不同。那些真正构建重要项目的人往往是高级员工，且在谷歌工作超过10年。相对"小"项目的员工往往更有趣，因为他们有机会从零开始构建并尝试有趣的项目。

• braza强调，在讨论复杂性时，需要区分可控的复杂性和固有的、环境导致的复杂性。虽然谷歌处理的问题很复杂，但在某些领域（如海运物流、制造业等）的复杂性可能更高且更难以解决。他提醒大家在阅读相关文章时要注意这些区别。

• neilv进一步探讨了这种自信的潜在问题，指出自信可能转变为自大或道德优越感，从而导致问题。他建议在尊重意志和努力的同时，也要尊重谦逊和真实性。

• ggm提到两个迷思：复杂系统 inherently 坏和简单系统 always 更好。他以武装部队和DNA为例，说明复杂性有时是必要的，且简单系统也可能包含未解的复杂性。

• 对文章写作质量的评论（carom）

• 谷歌开发经验的实际价值和其复杂系统的处理方式是否被过度高估。
• 复杂性和 complicated 之间的区别及如何在不同领域正确应用这些概念。
• 在处理复杂系统时，自信与谦逊之间的平衡如何把握。

Hello! Today, let’s discuss a fascinating topic: complex systems.
Introduction
Throughout my career, I’ve worked in many complicated environments. For instance, I worked on optimizing driver-passenger matching in ride-hailing at a Uber's competitor. This context, like others, was technically challenging. Yet, nothing comes close in terms of complexity with my current experience at Google and two years there have refined my perception of complexity.
In this post, we will break down the very concept of complexity. Next, we will take a step back to understand what makes certain environments rather complex than complicated and then explore patterns for navigating complex systems effectively.
Complicated vs. Complex
Understanding the distinction between complicated and complex problems is crucial because each requires a fundamentally different approach:
Complicated problems are intricate but predictable
. They followed structured, repeatable solutions. For example, filing taxes is complicated, but it's a structured and conventional problem since the process remains mostly the same year after year.
Complex problems are intricate but unique
. They require adaptive and often novel solutions. For example, climate change mitigation is a complex problem because it requires new and adaptive solutions and existing methods alone can’t really address its evolving challenges.
Back to software engineering, at the Uber competitor,
one of the challenges was to efficiently find the nearest driver for a passenger
. This was far from trivial, but it wasn't
complex
per se. Indeed, many solutions exist, such as applying geo-hashing (
example
), and implementing one of these solutions was the right approach.
At Google, I work as a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), focusing on the systems powering Google’s ML infrastructure. Here,
I consider the challenges genuinely complex
, as new paradigms and scheduling approaches are required, especially at Google’s scale.
Recognizing whether a system is complicated or complex is really important. Indeed, we mentioned that complicated systems are by definition repeatable, while complex systems require unique and customized approaches. Therefore, if we try to apply a common solution to a complex problem,
it may not lead to effective results
.
Characteristics of Complex Systems
In this section, we will discuss five common characteristics that help identify complex systems. Not all complex systems share every characteristic, but they tend to exhibit at least some of the following.
Emergent Behavior
Emergent behavior arises when a system's overall behavior
cannot be predicted solely by analyzing its individual components in isolation
.
For example, Gemini producing
unexpected results
was an emergent behavior. While I can't disclose the root cause, this behavior was nearly impossible to foresee by analyzing all the different components separately.
This is one possible characteristic of complex systems: they behave in ways that can hardly be predicted just by looking at their parts, making them harder to debug and manage.
Delayed Consequences
Another possible characteristic of complex systems is delayed consequences, where actions
don't always have immediate effects
, and instead, consequences may only become apparent much later.
For example, deploying a new version of a system might introduce a subtle issue that only appears days or even weeks later. This delay complicates debugging since identifying the root cause becomes much harder compared to immediate impacts.
In complex systems, relying solely on immediate feedback can create a false sense of stability, leading to major surprises when an issue finally emerges. Keeping in mind that consequences may take time to surface is essential when working in such environments.
Local vs. Global Optimization
In complex systems,
optimizing one part doesn’t necessarily improve the whole system
, and in some cases, it can even make things worse.
Unlike in non-complex systems, where improving one part generally leads to positive gains, complex systems are much more difficult to reason about. The components interact in non-obvious ways, and local optimizations can create ripple effects that are difficult to predict, sometimes leading to negative outcomes at the system level.
This highlights a key trait of complex systems: the whole is more than the sum of its parts. As a result, local gains don’t always translate into global improvements and in some cases, they can even degrade the overall system.
Hysteresis
Hysteresis describes how a system's
past state continues to influence its behavior
, even after the original cause is removed.

data.title: Lightweight open source reCaptcha alternative
data.author: michalpleban
data.article_summary: ALTCHA 是一个自托管的 CAPTCHA 替代方案，利用工作量证明（PoW）机制保护网站和在线服务免受垃圾信息和滥用。它不依赖 cookies 或指纹识别，确保用户隐私，并符合 GDPR、WCAG 2.2 AA 标准以及欧洲无障碍法案（EAA）。其特点包括无摩擦的用户体验、无 cookie 设计、完全无障碍、轻量级（GZIP 压缩后仅 17 kB）、自托管以及提供 SaaS 选项。安装和使用简单，支持多种前端和后端技术，并可通过配置实现多种功能。与 hCaptcha 和 reCAPTCHA 相比，ALTCHA 的体积更小，性能更优。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CAPTCHA系统的有效性、技术实现及其问题

不同观点：
• [binary132] 认为互联网和应用程序栈过度依赖专有托管服务，这些服务可能会随时间消失或失效。依赖第三方服务的功能性存在风险，尤其是当这些服务中断或改变时。专有软件即使可以自行操作，也仍然不如能够“自行修复设备”的开源方案。

• [serhack_] 提出有效的CAPTCHA类系统应通过收集大量数据、识别可疑模式并验证这些模式来动态生成挑战。例如，如果系统识别出用户是机器人，它会提供计算量更大的挑战，以增加机器人操作的难度。

• [remram] 质疑现代CAPTCHA系统是否真的在区分计算机和人类，认为它们只是在区分人类浏览器和机器人浏览器，甚至可能只是减慢所有浏览器的速度。

• [dankobgd] 认为reCAPTCHA系统不仅无用，还会惹恼真实用户，并分享了自己在使用MIUI网站时遇到的麻烦经历，暗示这些系统可能只是为了收集用户数据。

• [Jleagle] 提问为什么机器人不能计算工作量证明（PoW），暗示如果机器人能够计算PoW，那么这种CAPTCHA机制可能无效。

• [pabs3] 关心如果没有设置cookie，系统如何知道用户已经计算了PoW，或者是否每次页面加载都需要重新计算。

• [rahimnathwani] 询问是否有实时演示，以便更好地理解所讨论的CAPTCHA系统如何工作。

• [progx] 提出在人工智能时代，如何检测真实人类和AI的问题，暗示传统CAPTCHA可能无法应对AI的挑战。

• [chrismorgan] 详细分析CAPTCHA的演变，指出它已经偏离了原本区分计算机和人类的目标，变成了仅仅是增加攻击成本的机制。讨论了SHA哈希作为PoW机制的潜在问题，特别是针对专业硬件的优势，认为这种机制最终可能无法抵挡强大的攻击者。同时，指出大多数机器人仍然非常愚蠢，简单的防御措施可能已经足够。

• [immibis] 讽刺reCAPTCHA的目的是增强Google用户档案和拒绝合法用户，暗示所讨论的替代方案可能没有解决这些问题，并提到传统CAPTCHA收集大量指纹数据以确保只有特定配置的用户可以访问网站。

补充讨论：
- CAPTCHA系统的有效性和其技术实现，包括PoW的具体机制和潜在漏洞。
- 讨论了专有托管服务和专有软件的长期可靠性问题。
- 对现代CAPTCHA系统是否真正实现其宣称目标的质疑和批评。
- 关于如何在人工智能时代有效区分人类和机器人的开放性问题。

ALTCHA
ALTCHA leverages a proof-of-work mechanism to safeguard your website, APIs, and online services from spam and abuse. Unlike traditional solutions, ALTCHA is self-hosted, does not rely on cookies or fingerprinting, and ensures complete user privacy. It is fully compliant with

Lightweight
: Minimal bundle size for fast page loads and optimal performance.
Self-Hosted
: Operates independently without depending on third-party services.

data.title: Moving Forth: a series on writing Forth kernels
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文列出了Bradford J. Rodriguez发表的各类论文、研讨会、计算机程序，涵盖Forth内核设计、多任务处理、多处理器系统、专家控制系统等主题。主要系列包括《Moving Forth》系列，详细讲解Forth内核设计及其实现；多篇关于多任务和多处理器系统的文章，如《Multiprocessing for the Impoverished》系列；以及1997年博士论文《An Embedded Temporal Expert For Control of a Tandem Accelerator》和1989年硕士论文《PatternForth: A Pattern-Matching Language for Real-Time Control》。此外，还包括关于Forth汇编器、模式匹配语言、MIDI控制器等主题的杂文和计算机程序代码，如CamelForth在不同处理器上的实现。所有内容均附带文本、图片及相关链接，部分为PDF格式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Forth编程语言及其相关资源、工具的使用和学习难点

不同观点：
• [benji-york] 认为该系列标题参考了1981年的书籍《Starting FORTH》，并提供了一个在线阅读链接。他建议阅读这本书的几章内容，认为这对学习Forth有帮助。
• [zck] 表示自己在编写Forth时遇到了设计限制不同于传统指南的困难。由于使用C语言而不是汇编，他感到学习汇编比较困难，且C语言不能像汇编那样直接跳转代码。他还提到理解底层信息（如变量`w`的用途和寄存器使用）的挑战，并有意制作一系列图表来更好地理解Forth的程序流程。
• [anthk] 分享了一个GitHub上的Forth相关项目（subleq），并提供了使用说明。他还提到另一个工具（muxleq），并指出其在不同操作系统上的编译和使用方法。他通过具体例子展示了如何运行和测试Forth代码，并分享了在这些工具上获得的性能体验。

补充讨论：
• [zck] 的评论中提到了学习Forth的具体困难，包括语言的底层细节和程序流的理解问题，这与其他评论中分享资源和工具的使用形成对比。
• [anthk] 的评论更侧重于实际操作和工具使用，提供了详细的步骤和性能比较，显示出对Forth在不同平台上运行的实际体验的关注。
• 争议的焦点可能在于Forth学习的难度和方法。例如，[zck] 觉得从汇编学习Forth比较困难，而[benji-york] 则建议通过阅读经典书籍来学习。同时，[anthk] 提供了一种通过实际项目和工具来实践学习的途径。

总结：讨论围绕Forth编程的学习资源、工具使用及实际编程中的挑战展开，参与者分享了各自的经验和见解。

data.title: Fast machines, slow machines (2023)
data.author: amatheus
data.article_summary: 作者意外地因一段对比旧电脑（运行Windows NT 3.51）和新电脑（运行Windows 11）应用打开速度的视频而走红。旧电脑（AMD K7-600）尽管硬件过时，但应用启动迅速；而新电脑（Surface Go 2）尽管硬件更强大，却表现出明显的延迟。作者承认最初对比不公平，因旧电脑硬件相对其系统过于强大，且错误引用了新电脑的硬件规格。在重新对比（Windows 2000与Windows 11，使用合理配置）后，旧系统在界面响应速度上仍占优势。作者认为，现代计算机在界面延迟方面表现不佳，尽管新系统在其他方面有显著进步，但这一问题值得关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件性能问题及其原因

不同观点：
• 作者[jmmv]认为，现代操作系统（如Windows 11和macOS）在高端硬件上仍然表现迟缓，尤其是与KDE等桌面环境相比。他指出，即使是简单的应用程序（如Notepad的重写版）也变得更慢，并将其归因于软件开发中对性能问题的忽视。
• 用户[maccard]不同意将性能问题完全归咎于.NET重写，并以Unity和Mono为例，说明某些技术即便使用较老版本仍然表现良好。他认为，问题可能出在现代应用程序框架和操作系统设计上。
• 用户[sshine]指出，过去程序员更注重性能是因为进入编程领域的门槛较高，而现在商业激励促使开发者推出半成品并忽视修复问题。
• 用户[bigstrat2003]认为，软件开发组织优先考虑开发便利性和利润，而非产品质量，导致软件质量下降。他认为开源社区是唯一可靠的高质量软件来源。

• 用户[vanschelven]和[jonathanlydall]提供了外部链接和具体例子（如Google Authenticator的延迟问题）来支持讨论。

• 用户[chrsw]用一句引用表达对软件性能问题的失望情绪。

• 软件性能问题的主要原因：是特定技术选择（如.NET重写）还是整体开发和设计问题。

43972004.article_content:
Well,
that
was unexpected. I recorded a couple of crappy videos in 5 minutes,
posted them on a Twitter thread
, and went viral with 8.8K likes at this point. I really could not have predicted that, given that I’ve been posting what-I-believe-is interesting content for years and… nothing, almost-zero interest. Now that things have cooled down, it’s time to stir the pot and elaborate on those thoughts a bit more rationally.
To summarize, the Twitter thread shows two videos: one of an old computer running Windows NT 3.51 and one of a new computer running Windows 11. In each video, I opened and closed a command prompt, File Explorer, Notepad, and Paint. You can clearly see how apps on the old computer open up instantly whereas apps on the new computer show significant lag as they load. I questioned how computers are actually getting better when trivial things like this have regressed. And boom, the likes and reshares started coming in. Obviously some people had issues with my claims, but there seems to be an overwhelming majority of people that agree we have a problem.
To open up, I’ll stand my ground: latency in modern computer interfaces, with modern OSes and modern applications, is terrible and getting worse. This applies to smartphones as well. At the same time, while UIs were much more responsible on computers of the past, those computers were also awful in many ways: new systems have changed our lives substantially. So, what gives?
A blog on operating systems, programming languages, testing, build systems, my own software
projects and even personal productivity. Specifics include FreeBSD, Linux, Rust, Bazel and
EndBASIC.
Subscribe
0
subscribers
The original comparison
Let’s address the elephant in the room first. The initial comparison I posted
wasn’t
fair and I was aware of that going in. That said, I
knew
repeating the experiment “properly” would yield the same results, so I plowed ahead with whatever I had right then. The videos were unplanned because the idea for the Tweets came to mind when I booted the old machine, clicked on Command Prompt, and was blown away by the immediacy to start the app.
The original comparison videos showed:
An AMD K7-600 with 128MB of RAM and a 5400 RPM HDD running Windows NT 3.51. This was a machine from the year 1999-2000 with an OS that was about 5 years older than it. Hardware was experiencing really fast improvements back then, particularly in CPU speeds, and you were kinda expected to keep up with the 2-year upgrade treadmill or suffer from incredibly slowness. All this is to say that this machine was indeed overpowered for the OS I used.
Please remind me how we are moving forward. In this video, a machine from the year ~2000 (600MHz, 128MB RAM, spinning-rust hard disk) running Windows NT 3.51. Note how incredibly snappy opening apps is. 👇
pic.twitter.com/YEO824vIqI
— Julio Merino (@jmmv)
June 22, 2023
A Surface Go 2 with an Intel Core m3 CPU, 8GB of RAM, and an SSD running Windows 11. This is a 3-year old machine that shipped with Windows 10, but Windows 11 is officially supported on it—and as you know, that means you are tricked into upgrading. This is
not
a powerful machine by any means, but: first, it’s running the verbatim Microsoft experience, and second, it
should
be much more powerful than the K7 system, shouldn’t it? We are continuously reminded that any computer or phone today has orders of magnitude more power than past machines.
Now look at opening the same apps on Windows 11 on a Surface Go 2 (quad-core i5 processor at 2.4GHz, 8GB RAM, SSD). Everything is super sluggish.
pic.twitter.com/W722PNEGv0
— Julio Merino (@jmmv)
June 22, 2023
Oh, and yes, I quoted the wrong hardware specs in the original tweet. Looking again on how I made that mistake: I searched for “Surface Go 2” in Bing, I landed on the “Surface
Laptop
Go 2” page, and copied what I saw there without noticing that it wasn’t accurate.
All apps had been previously open, so they should all have been comfortably sitting in RAM.
The better comparison
Obviously various people noticed that there was something off with my comparison (unfair hardware configurations, wrong specs), so I redid the comparison once the thread started gaining attention:
Windows 2000 on the K7-600 machine (see
installation thread
). This is an OS from 1999 running on hardware from that same year. And, if you ask me, this was the best Windows release of all times: super-clean UI on an NT core, carrying all of the features you would want around performance and stability (except with terrible boot times). As you can see, things still fare
very
well for the old machine in terms of UI responsiveness.
For those thinking that the comparison was unfair, here is Windows 2000 on the same 600MHz machine. Both are from the same year, 1999. Note how the immediacy is still exactly the same and hadn’t been ruined yet.
pic.twitter.com/Tpks2Hd1Id
— Julio Merino (@jmmv)
June 23, 2023
Windows 11 on a Mac Pro 2013 (see
installation instructions
)

data.title: In the US, a rotating detonation rocket engine takes flight
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: Venus Aerospace, a US-based propulsion company, has successfully tested a rotating detonation rocket engine, marking the first such flight in the US. The engine, which has been a topic of academic discussion for decades, operates by creating a detonation wave that travels around a circular channel, increasing fuel efficiency. The test, conducted in New Mexico, used a small rocket powered by a 2,000-pound thrust engine and lasted about 30 seconds. CEO Sassie Duggleby described the flight as "historic," noting its potential to enable hypersonic travel, allowing global journeys in under two hours. While the long-term goal is to develop hypersonic aircraft, Venus is currently focusing on near-term opportunities in commercial and defense applications, with support from both government and commercial sectors.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：旋转爆震发动机（RDE）的原理、应用、技术挑战及其实际意义

不同观点：
• ColinWright：对旋转爆震发动机的基本原理表示困惑，通过外部链接和维基百科进行查询和理解，初步认识到RDE的效率优势和潜在缺点（如不稳定性和噪音）。
• verzali：对RDE的商业应用（如Venus Aerospace的超音速客机计划）表示质疑，认为其更可能吸引军方的兴趣和资助，而非商业旅行市场。
• Havoc：对RDE中爆炸产生的应力表示担忧，质疑其是否会引起结构问题，或者是否有多重爆炸在相对侧同步发生。
• pgruenbacher：提供了一个包含可视化内容的网络研讨会链接，帮助其他人更好地理解RDE的概念。
• superkuh：认为RDE是少数真正具有潜力的高超音速技术之一，能够通过加速燃烧过程和增加射程来简化飞行器设计，避免空气呼吸问题和过高的热负荷。
• ashoeafoot：提出RDE在熄火后如何重启的实际操作问题。
• lupusreal：通过JAXA在2021年试飞RDE的例子，提示该技术的发展速度。
• casey2：对RDE的实际意义表示怀疑，认为即使爆炸率为0%，总旅行时间可能仍然更长。
• aaron695：提供了Venus Aerospace的视频链接，指出其技术性极强，包含大量方程和专业内容。
• growlNark：认为“高超音速”是一个没有实际意义的术语，暗示其只是超音速的不同程度，并指出该术语被军方滥用。

补充讨论：
• RDE的效率和潜在缺点：ColinWright引用的维基百科内容指出RDE在理论上比传统燃烧方式效率高25%，但存在不稳定性和噪音问题。
• RDE的军事与商业应用：verzali认为RDE更可能用于军事而非商业旅行，这引发了对该技术实际应用场景的讨论。
• RDE的应力与结构问题：Havoc担心RDE中的爆炸会产生巨大应力，对结构稳定性构成威胁，但未有明确答案。
• RDE的可视化与理解：pgruenbacher提供的视频链接帮助其他人更好地理解RDE的原理和实际运行方式。
• RDE的重启问题：ashoeafoot提出了RDE在实际操作中可能遇到的熄火重启问题，这是一个值得注意的技术挑战。
• RDE的发展现状：lupusreal通过JAXA的试飞例子提示了该技术的发展速度，表明其已经进入实际测试阶段。
• RDE的实际意义与命名争议：casey2和growlNark对RDE的实际意义和技术术语的准确性提出了质疑，认为需要更明确的定义和解释。

争议焦点：
• RDE的主要应用场景：verzali认为更适合军事而非商业，其他参与者未明确回应但提供了相关信息。
• RDE的实际效率与可行性：casey2对RDE的实际效果表示怀疑，而superkuh则强调其技术潜力，形成了对该技术前景的不同看法。
• “高超音速”术语的准确性：growlNark认为该术语被滥用，而其他参与者未直接回应此观点。

A US-based propulsion company, Venus Aerospace, said Wednesday it had completed a short flight test of its rotating detonation rocket engine at Spaceport America in New Mexico.
The company's chief executive and co-founder, Sassie Duggleby, characterized the flight as "historic." It is believed to be the first US-based flight test of an idea that has been discussed academically for decades, a rotating detonation rocket engine. The concept has previously been tested in a handful of other countries, but never with a high-thrust engine.
"By proving this engine works beyond the lab, Venus brings the world closer to a future where hypersonic travel—traversing the globe in under two hours—becomes possible," Duggleby told Ars.
A quick flight
The company has only released limited information about the test. The small rocket, powered by the company's 2,000-pound thrust engine, launched from a rail in New Mexico. The vehicle flew for about half a minute, and, as planned, did not break the sound barrier.
Governments around the world have been interested in rotating detonation engine technology for a long time because it has the potential to significantly increase fuel efficiency in a variety of applications, from Navy carriers to rocket engines.
In contrast to a traditional rocket engine, in which a highly pressurized propellant and an oxidizer are injected into a combustion chamber where they burn and produce an energetic exhaust plume, a rotating detonation engine is different in that a wave of detonation travels around a circular channel. This is sustained by the injection of fuel and oxidizer and produces a shockwave that travels outward at supersonic speed.
Sassie Duggleby and her husband, Andrew Duggleby, founded Venus Aerospace nearly five years ago with the long-term goal of developing powerful rotating detonation engines and building a hypersonic aircraft that could carry perhaps a dozen passengers and travel at astonishingly fast speeds worldwide.
Aiming for hypersonics in the near term
Such a prospect is many years into the future, however. In the meantime, Venus is looking at more near-term opportunities and revenue sources. The company is seeking to position itself as a leader in affordable hypersonic flight for commercial and defense applications.
"It is vital for US interests that the government continues to fund efforts to maintain America’s economic competitiveness and national security," Sassie Duggleby said. "Hypersonics is one of the critical technologies to remain ahead of our national competitors. We’re fortunate to have robust interest from both government and commercial sectors."
Sassie Duggleby said Venus cannot disclose specific customers yet.
"We're actively engaged with US defense and national security agencies as well as commercial partners exploring hypersonic applications in logistics, aerospace, and future mobility—including large primes," she said. "The enthusiasm we’re seeing reflects a broad recognition that Venus’s technology can unlock new operational and economic possibilities across multiple markets."
Venus has a long way to go to reach its ultimate goal of highly efficient, hypersonic commercial flight. But the engine that flew this week is a good start toward proving that such a future, at least, is possible.

• ColinWright：对旋转爆震发动机的基本原理表示困惑，通过外部链接和维基百科进行查询和理解，初步认识到RDE的效率优势和潜在缺点（如不稳定性和噪音）。
• verzali：对RDE的商业应用（如Venus Aerospace的超音速客机计划）表示质疑，认为其更可能吸引军方的兴趣和资助，而非商业旅行市场。
• Havoc：对RDE中爆炸产生的应力表示担忧，质疑其是否会引起结构问题，或者是否有多重爆炸在相对侧同步发生。
• pgruenbacher：提供了一个包含可视化内容的网络研讨会链接，帮助其他人更好地理解RDE的概念。
• superkuh：认为RDE是少数真正具有潜力的高超音速技术之一，能够通过加速燃烧过程和增加射程来简化飞行器设计，避免空气呼吸问题和过高的热负荷。
• ashoeafoot：提出RDE在熄火后如何重启的实际操作问题。
• lupusreal：通过JAXA在2021年试飞RDE的例子，提示该技术的发展速度。
• casey2：对RDE的实际意义表示怀疑，认为即使爆炸率为0%，总旅行时间可能仍然更长。
• aaron695：提供了Venus Aerospace的视频链接，指出其技术性极强，包含大量方程和专业内容。
• growlNark：认为“高超音速”是一个没有实际意义的术语，暗示其只是超音速的不同程度，并指出该术语被军方滥用。

补充讨论：
• RDE的效率和潜在缺点：ColinWright引用的维基百科内容指出RDE在理论上比传统燃烧方式效率高25%，但存在不稳定性和噪音问题。
• RDE的军事与商业应用：verzali认为RDE更可能用于军事而非商业旅行，这引发了对该技术实际应用场景的讨论。
• RDE的应力与结构问题：Havoc担心RDE中的爆炸会产生巨大应力，对结构稳定性构成威胁，但未有明确答案。
• RDE的可视化与理解：pgruenbacher提供的视频链接帮助其他人更好地理解RDE的原理和实际运行方式。
• RDE的重启问题：ashoeafoot提出了RDE在实际操作中可能遇到的熄火重启问题，这是一个值得注意的技术挑战。
• RDE的发展现状：lupusreal通过JAXA的试飞例子提示了该技术的发展速度，表明其已经进入实际测试阶段。
• RDE的实际意义与命名争议：casey2和growlNark对RDE的实际意义和技术术语的准确性提出了质疑，认为需要更明确的定义和解释。

争议焦点：
• RDE的主要应用场景：verzali认为更适合军事而非商业，其他参与者未明确回应但提供了相关信息。
• RDE的实际效率与可行性：casey2对RDE的实际效果表示怀疑，而superkuh则强调其技术潜力，形成了对该技术前景的不同看法。
• “高超音速”术语的准确性：growlNark认为该术语被滥用，而其他参与者未直接回应此观点。

data.author: anomancer
data.article_summary: Boltzmann Machines是1980年代引入的生成型AI模型，用于无监督学习，可以从数据中学习而无需明确指示。它们由可见和隐藏神经元组成，通过能量函数进行训练，目标是最小化训练数据的能量。一般Boltzmann Machine神经元间全连接，训练复杂度高。Restricted Boltzmann Machine（RBM）则限制可见与隐藏神经元间的连接，训练更快。RBM通过对比散度（Contrastive Divergence）方法训练，包括钳制可见单元、采样隐藏单元、更新权重等步骤。最终，RBM可以从学习到的分布中生成与训练数据类似的新数据。文章还提供了一个浏览器中运行的RBM模拟器以展示训练过程。

总体来看，讨论涵盖了技术细节、历史背景、实际应用和用户体验等多方面内容。

LiveSplat
is an algorithm for realtime Gaussian splatting using RGBD camera streams. Join our
discord
for discussion and help. Check out the demo video below to see the the type of output that LiveSplat produces.
LiveSplat_Alexa.mp4
Message from the Author
LiveSplat was developed as a small part of a larger proprietary VR telerobotics system. I posted a video of the Gaussian splatting component of this system on Reddit and many people expressed an interest in experimenting with it themselves. So I spun it out and I'm making it publicly available as LiveSplat (see installation instructions below).
LiveSplat should be considered alpha quality. I do not have the resources to test the installation on many different machines, so let me know if the application does not run on yours (assuming your machine meets the requirements).
I've decided to keep LiveSplat closed source in order to explore potential business opportunities. If you are a business wanting to license/integrate this technology, please email
mark@axby.cc
.
I hope you have fun with LiveSplat!
— Mark Liu
Requirements
Python 3.12+
Windows or Ubuntu (other Linux distributions may work, but are untested)
x86_64 CPU
Nvidia graphics card
One or more (up to four) RGBD sensors
Installation
Note that the application is not open source, and is covered by this
license
.
Ubuntu:
pip install https://livesplat.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/livesplat-0.1.0-cp312-cp312-manylinux_x86_64.whl
Windows:
pip install https://livesplat.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/livesplat-0.1.0-cp312-cp312-win_amd64.whl
Running
To run LiveSplat, you will have to create an integration script that feeds your RGBD streams to the LiveSplat viewer. This repo provides an integration script for Intel Realsense devices called
livesplat_realsense.py
.

data.article_summary:
**llm-min.txt: 技术文档的Min.js风格压缩用于LLM上下文**

**简介**  
llm-min.txt是一个社区驱动的项目，旨在解决AI编码助手（如GitHub Copilot）因“知识截止”导致无法获取最新库信息的难题。传统方法如llms.txt和Context7存在文件过大或不透明的问题。

**llm-min.txt的创新**  
受JavaScript中min.js文件启发，llm-min.txt通过AI提炼技术文档，生成高度浓缩、结构化的摘要，专为AI优化而非人类阅读。该文件采用结构化知识格式（SKF），包含头部元数据和三大核心部分：定义、用法和关系。

**SKF格式关键元素**  
1. **头部元数据**：包括格式标识、文档来源、生成时间、主命名空间等。
2. **核心部分**：
   - **定义部分**：描述库的静态组件，如类、方法、属性等。

What is
llm-min.txt
and Why is it Important?
If you've ever used an AI coding assistant (like GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or others powered by Large Language Models - LLMs), you've likely encountered situations where they don't know about the latest updates to programming libraries. This knowledge gap exists because AI models have a "knowledge cutoff" – a point beyond which they haven't learned new information. Since software evolves rapidly, this limitation can lead to outdated recommendations and broken code.
Several innovative approaches have emerged to address this challenge:
llms.txt
A community-driven initiative where contributors create reference files (
llms.txt
) containing up-to-date library information specifically formatted for AI consumption.
Context7
A service that dynamically provides contextual information to AIs, often by intelligently summarizing documentation.
While these solutions are valuable, they face certain limitations:
llms.txt
files can become extraordinarily large – some exceeding
800,000
tokens (word fragments). This size can overwhelm many AI systems' context windows.
Many shorter
llms.txt
variants simply contain links to official documentation, requiring the AI to fetch and process those documents separately. Even the comprehensive versions (
llms-full.txt
) often exceed what most AI assistants can process at once. Additionally, these files may not always reflect the absolute latest documentation.
Context7
operates somewhat as a "black box" – while useful, its precise information selection methodology isn't fully transparent to users. It primarily works with GitHub code repositories or existing
llms.txt
files, rather than any arbitrary software package.
llm-min.txt
offers a fresh approach:
Inspired by
min.js
files in web development (JavaScript with unnecessary elements removed),
llm-min.txt
adopts a similar philosophy for technical documentation. Instead of feeding an AI a massive, verbose manual, we leverage another AI to distill that documentation into a super-condensed, highly structured summary. The resulting
llm-min.txt
file captures only the most essential information needed to understand a library's usage, packaged in a format optimized for AI assistants rather than human readers.
Modern AI reasoning capabilities excel at this distillation process, creating remarkably efficient knowledge representations that deliver maximum value with minimal token consumption.
Understanding
llm-min.txt
: A Machine-Optimized Format 🧩
The
llm-min.txt
file utilizes the
Structured Knowledge Format (SKF)
– a compact, machine-optimized format designed for efficient AI parsing rather than human readability. This format organizes technical information into distinct, highly structured sections with precise relationships.
Key Elements of the SKF Format:
Header Metadata:
Every file begins with essential contextual information:
# IntegratedKnowledgeManifest_SKF
: Format identifier and version
# SourceDocs: [...]
: Original documentation sources
# GenerationTimestamp: ...
: Creation timestamp
# PrimaryNamespace: ...
: Top-level package/namespace, critical for understanding import paths
Three Core Structured Sections:
The content is organized into distinct functional categories:
# SECTION: DEFINITIONS (Prefix: D)
: Describes the static aspects of the library:
Canonical component definitions with unique global IDs (e.g.,
D001:G001_MyClass
)
Namespace paths relative to
PrimaryNamespace
Method signatures with parameters and return types
Properties/fields with types and access modifiers
Static relationships like inheritance or interface implementation

**llm-min.txt: 技术文档的Min.js风格压缩用于LLM上下文**

**简介**  
llm-min.txt是一个社区驱动的项目，旨在解决AI编码助手（如GitHub Copilot）因“知识截止”导致无法获取最新库信息的难题。传统方法如llms.txt和Context7存在文件过大或不透明的问题。

**llm-min.txt的创新**  
受JavaScript中min.js文件启发，llm-min.txt通过AI提炼技术文档，生成高度浓缩、结构化的摘要，专为AI优化而非人类阅读。该文件采用结构化知识格式（SKF），包含头部元数据和三大核心部分：定义、用法和关系。

**SKF格式关键元素**  
1. **头部元数据**：包括格式标识、文档来源、生成时间、主命名空间等。
2. **核心部分**：
   - **定义部分**：描述库的静态组件，如类、方法、属性等。
   - **用法部分**：包含代码示例和使用说明。
   - **关系部分**：展示组件间的动态关系，如继承或接口实现。

**优势**  
llm-min.txt通过精简文档，使AI助手能在有限上下文窗口内高效处理最新技术信息，同时保持高准确性。

data.title: How we made billing backendless
data.author: ayushrodrigues
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了Autumn团队尝试将支付和账单处理移到前端，以提供更好的开发者体验。最初，他们引入了一个"可发布密钥"（publishable key），让开发者可以直接在前端处理支付链接和检查功能访问权限，但发现该方案存在局限性和安全隐患。接着，他们尝试使用Next.js的服务器动作（server actions）来实现，但由于未认证的公共路由导致安全问题。最终，他们通过加密客户ID解决了部分安全问题，但意识到这种方法仅适用于支持服务器动作的框架。作者承认，未来可能放弃这种方法，转向更框架无关的方案，简化后端路由设置，使集成更加标准化和安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“无后端计费”方案的可行性、安全性及其实际应用的讨论

不同观点：
• **Daviey**：认为“无后端计费”突显了开发体验（DX）与安全性之间的矛盾。虽然减少后端模板代码有吸引力，但安全性问题不可避免。特别是服务器操作中的IDOR漏洞（不安全的直接对象引用）是一个严重问题，仅靠前端无法解决。最终结论是，传统的“后端路由加认证”方法存在是有理由的。

• **biker142541**：对“无后端计费”的概念感到困惑，认为如果需要服务器操作，那就不是真正的无后端。建议更清晰地说明只是简化了后端交互，而不是完全去除后端。

• **taurath**：同样对文章感到不解，质疑为何计费需要webhooks和状态同步。认为可以在静态网站上接受支付而不需要webhooks，并提出这可能是在通过计费过程处理权限认证，而不是直接称之为认证。

• **beej71**：担心如果加密后的客户ID被获取，是否会导致客户被冒充。问题在于客户ID是否可被猜测，从而引发安全问题。

• **serbuvlad**：认为现代web技术越来越复杂且难以理解。强调任何支付处理都需要后端，所谓“无后端”只是混淆概念。同时也提到serverless实际上还是有服务器，只是形式不同。

• **singron**：提出服务器操作为何不能被认证，认为这是明显的解决方案。还提到密钥轮换和过期机制的问题，指出如果不解决这些问题，最终可能会重新发明类似JWT的机制。

• **robertlagrant**：建议直接对用户进行认证，然后可以安全地传递客户ID或使用替代键。提出可以使用JWT来实现这一点，特别是在无服务器函数中。

• **baobun**：认为团队正在重新发明JWT，建议深入了解JWT及其功能。

• **oulipo**：批评文章中的工程师缺乏基本的安全知识，指出多次事后才意识到方案不安全，令人担忧。

• **codegeek**：指出YC投资了类似的公司，useautumn与另一家YC公司getlago是直接竞争对手。

• **throwaway63467**：质疑服务器操作是否本身就是后端，认为如果需要服务器操作，那就不算是无后端。

• **delusional**：质疑在没有后端的情况下如何确保计费的准确性。提出用户可以通过控制台调用函数或修改代码，认为大多数多人在线游戏已经通过服务器权威模拟解决了类似问题。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于“无后端计费”是否可行及安全，特别是如何处理认证和授权问题。
- 多次提到JWT作为解决方案或类似概念，表明JWT在这种场景下的适用性和普遍性。
- 对“无后端”这一术语的混淆和质疑贯穿评论，反映出对新概念的理解和接受程度不一。
- 强调了安全性的重要性，尤其是在处理支付和客户数据时，不能仅依赖前端解决方案。

How we made billing backendless
Ayush, Autumn Co-Founder
We think handling payments on the frontend is a better developer experience.
Typically, billing is a backend job and requires webhooks, state syncing, then passing the data to the frontend. We wanted to offer a more "out-of-the-box" experience when handling things like payment links, paywalls and up/downgrade flows, and spent a bunch of time thinking about how we can perform sensitive operations without needing to perform the "round trip" to the backend.
This is a short write up of our exploration around the problem and why we ultimately are giving up.
Part 1: The Publishable Key
When we launched, we had a secret key that could be used securely from the backend just as Stripe does. Many of our first users had actually never set up Stripe before, and immediately told us they wish they could just do it from the frontend.
Our first solution was to create a "publishable key" which would let developers get payment links and check feature access (eg, does my user have any remaining credits) directly from the frontend, in an unprotected way. These functions alone can't really be abused.
The initial response was good and people were happy to use it with their initial set up. But we quickly ran into a couple problems:
It only worked with some endpoints (eg, tracking billable usage events had to be done via the secret key) and ended up confusing devs around which endpoints could be used with which keys.
Most software billing flows allow you to automatically purchase something if you've made a purchase before. This automatic purchasing (eg for upgrades) definitely couldn't be done with a public key.
Although it helped people spin up a sample integration fast, it quickly had to be ripped out anyway, so ended up being pretty pointless.
This still exists in our docs today and constantly trips people up. Can't wait to get rid of it.
Part 2: Server Actions
When we launched our Next.js library, we were excited to use server actions. The DX felt magical because users could:
Call them from the frontend like any normal function
The functions run on the server and can access our secret key stored as an ENV variable
No route set up needed, and the request is secure â nice!
Unfortunately we soon discovered our approach was flawed. Server actions are public, unauthenticated routes, and our API calls updates resources based on a
customer_id
field (eg. upgrade / downgrade requests, tracking usage for a feature, etc).
So if you got a hold of someone elseâs customer ID, you could make requests to the public server actions as if you were that customerâmaking this method insecure.
Part 3: Server actions + encryption
We really really liked the DX of server actions though, and so we had to brainstorm a way to overcome the customer ID being expoed in server action routes.
A few options came to mind, like using a middleware, or registering an authentication function, but the cleanest and simplest method we thought of was simply encrypting the customer ID:
Hereâs how it worked:
Our Provider was a server component, and so itâd take in a customer ID/user ID (server side), encrypt it using their API key, and pass it to context on the client side (see image below)
We wrap each server action with a client side function which grabs the
encryptedCustomerId
from context and passes it to the server action. These are all exported through a hook â
useAutumn
Each server action first decrypts the customer ID then calls the Autumn API
Essentially, we baked our own layer of auth into the server actions, and this is how our Next.js library works today. I haven't seen this approach by anyone else but essentially lets us fully handle secure payments, upgrades, downgrades, usage-based billing events â all from the frontend.
Weâre still not fully satisfied since this only works with frameworks that support server actions and SPA / vite is kinda making a comeback. It also makes the implementation different across frameworks.
The future
Ultimately I think we'll reach a point where we give up on this approach, and move towards a more framework agnostic approach. Rather than trying to abandon the backend route setup, we'll just make it easy to do. Take better-auth and how they generate their backend routes in just a couple lines of code â theyâve standardised the backend and frontend installation, and is pretty hard to get wrong.
Other companies like Polar have a similar approach and are heavily praised for it. We probably don't need to reinvent the wheel (as fun as it is).
The easiest way to integrate Stripe âº

• **delusional**：质疑在没有后端的情况下如何确保计费的准确性。提出用户可以通过控制台调用函数或修改代码，认为大多数多人在线游戏已经通过服务器权威模拟解决了类似问题。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于“无后端计费”是否可行及安全，特别是如何处理认证和授权问题。
- 多次提到JWT作为解决方案或类似概念，表明JWT在这种场景下的适用性和普遍性。
- 对“无后端”这一术语的混淆和质疑贯穿评论，反映出对新概念的理解和接受程度不一。
- 强调了安全性的重要性，尤其是在处理支付和客户数据时，不能仅依赖前端解决方案。

data.title: Lua for Elixir
data.author: davydog187
data.article_summary:
2025年5月12日，Elixir库Lua发布了首个稳定版本v0.1.0，该库允许在BEAM VM上直接执行隔离的Lua程序，完全实现了Lua 5.3，而无需嵌入C语言的Lua运行时和编译器。这是通过Luerl库实现的，Luerl是用Erlang实现的Lua解析器、编译器和运行时。Lua Elixir库扩展了Luerl的功能，改进了错误信息并提供了详细的文档。主要功能包括通过`deflua`宏将Elixir API暴露给Lua，使用`~LUA`符号在编译时验证Lua语法，以及提供详细的文档和Livebook示例。

该库起源于TV Labs，用于执行任意代码以进行高层次的集成测试。未来计划包括改进Luerl的错误消息、文档和与Lua生态的深度集成，并计划合并Elixir Lua库到Luerl，发布2.0.0版本。感兴趣的开发者可以通过Slack、Discord参与或在Github上提交问题。

43972485.article_content:
Published
May 12, 2025
Introducing Lua for Elixir
The first stable release of the Elixir library,
Lua v0.1.0
, has been released to
hex.pm
!
Lua is a library that allows you to execute arbitrary, sandboxed
Lua
programs directly on the BEAM VM. This is
not
embedding the C Lua runtime and compiler, but rather a complete implementation of Lua 5.3. This feat is made possible by the underlying
Luerl library
, which implements a Lua parser, compiler, and runtime, all in Erlang.
The Lua Elixir library extends the capabilities of the Luerl library, improving error messages and providing robust documentation.
Feature highlights include:
Extending Lua with Elixir APIs
The Lua Elixir library has a
deflua
macro for easily expressing APIs in Elixir that can be exposed to Lua with
Lua.load_api/2
defmodule MyAPI do
use Lua.API
deflua double(v), do: 2 * v
end
import Lua, only: [sigil_LUA: 2]
lua = Lua.new() |> Lua.load_api(MyAPI)
{[10], _} = Lua.eval!(lua, ~LUA[return double(5)])
Compile-time syntax evaluation
A
~LUA
sigil is exposed, allowing the validation of Lua syntax at Elixir compile time.
iex> import Lua, only: [sigil_LUA: 2]
#iex> {[4], _} = Lua.eval!(~LUA[return 2 +])
** (Lua.CompilerException) Failed to compile Lua!
Robust documentation
See the
Lua Hex docs
for detailed documentation and examples for working with Lua and Luerl.
A
Livebook
is also available to get you started.
Born at TV Labs
The Lua Elixir library started as a proof of concept at
TV Labs
, where I am co-founder and CTO. At TV Labs, we needed to execute arbitrary code to allow our customers to write high-level integration tests against physical televisions and other streaming media devices. What started as a prototype led to diving deep into the particulars of Luerl, improving its usability and error messages, while making it easy to use from Elixir. TV Labs uses Lua as a compilation target for its
drag and drop Automation builder
, where users can specify the high-level workflow of their tests, and we handle the scheduling and underlying execution.
The Elixir Lua library and Luerl have allowed us to build a working solution for vision-based integration tests on physical devices, without needing to orchestrate additional Javascript or Python virtual machines, and executing the code on compute right next to the physical device.
How Luerl came to be
Robert Virding is a living legend. Beyond being a
famous movie star
, Robert is best known for collaborating with
Joe Armstrong
and Mike Williams at Ericsson in the mid-80s to create the
Erlang Programming Language
. Erlang is originally known for its use in telecommunications and its properties of fault-tolerance, concurrency, and immutable data, but is now regarded as a general purpose language, with its virtual machine, the BEAM VM, powering many languages including Elixir and Gleam. Since it wasn’t fun to just create
one
programming language, Robert also created
Lisp flavored Erlang (LFE)
, a Prolog interpreter in Erlang called
Erlog
, and of course, an implementation of Lua called
Luerl
.
During
Code BEAM EU 2024
, I had the honor of
giving a talk
with Robert. Since Luerl seemed to be a side project for him, I asked him why he bothered creating it in the first place. Robert smirked and said:
I wrote a Prolog on Erlang, that was fun. Then I wrote a functional Lisp in Erlang, that was fun too. But then I realized that it would be neat to implement an imperative or object-oriented language on the BEAM, so I picked Lua and had at it. That’s how Luerl was born.
If I’ve learned anything from this experience and collaborating with Robert, it’s that he still gets immense joy from creating and experimenting, and Luerl is one of those many examples.
The future of Lua and Luerl
Lua has been a great foundation for building our automation platform at TV Labs; however, there are many improvements needed in Luerl to make it more useful:
The quality of error messages needs to be dramatically improved
Stacktraces often lack useful context and information
Documentation and examples need significant work
Sandboxing features related to memory need more examination and exploration
Deeper integration with the larger Lua ecosystem
To that end, Robert and I have discussed merging the Elixir Lua library into Luerl. We hope to do this and release a 2.0.0 version of Luerl, continuing to improve documentation, remove deprecated interfaces, and dramatically improve error messages and stack traces.
If you’re interested in getting involved, join the
Slack
or
Discord
, or
open an issue on Github
.
Thanks!
See a mistake/bug? Edit this article on
Github

data.title: A Rust API Inspired by Python, Powered by Serde
data.author: lukastyrychtr
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了如何在Rust中实现类似于Python的动态API，特别是利用`serde`库来模拟Python的`__getattr__`功能。作者希望在Rust中创建一个用户友好的API，类似于Python中通过WMI包获取系统信息的简便方法。文章首先展示了Python中通过动态属性访问系统信息的代码，然后说明了如何在Rust中实现等效的“原始”API，但这种原始API使用起来较为繁琐，需要手动检查和处理各种数据类型。

为了改善用户体验，作者提出了一种受Python启发的设计，允许用户定义自定义结构体（如`Fan`），并通过泛型函数`query`返回这些结构体的实例。文章最后讨论了如何通过定义新trait来实现这一功能，使API更直观易用。这一设计的核心在于利用Rust的泛型和trait功能来实现类似于Python的动态行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对API设计和实现方式的不同看法，特别是围绕查询系统数据时的接口设计、优化以及类型安全等问题。

不同观点：
• dundarious认为原始的直接查询方式更好，理由是代码更小、更简单，并建议通过创建typedef来处理类型问题，而不是使用对象接口。他强调了简洁性和性能。
• dgacmu则支持使用对象接口，认为这样可以将限制条件更深地推入查询中，从而优化性能，特别是在处理大量数据时。
• throw_a_grenade提到Minijinja内部实现的方式，指出可以通过实现Deserialize接口来传递结构体并处理对象属性。
• ohr（本文作者）解释了使用Serde进行“反射”的初衷，并希望通过深入探讨Serde内部机制来引发读者兴趣。
• lnyng分享了一个类似的工具实现，强调了对类型安全和查询便捷性的需求，并提出了是否存在更简单的方法或现有proc宏来实现这一目标的疑问。
• xpe对文章标题和内容提出了批评，认为文章没有明确API的类型和要解决的问题，导致读者难以快速判断文章的价值。
• lovasoa主张使用方法而不是属性来实现查询接口，认为这样更整洁。
• vlovich123质疑本文提出的方法相对于Diesel.rs（一个更成熟的ORM库）的优势，指出Diesel具有更复杂的过滤、连接和支持多种SQL方言的能力。
• VWWHFSfQ建议使用turbofish语法来使代码更自然和透明。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点之一是直接查询与对象接口查询之间的选择，前者强调简洁和性能，后者注重优化和可扩展性。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对类型安全的关注，特别是在查询嵌套结构体字段时，如何实现更简便和类型安全的查询方法。
- 对文章标题和内容的清晰度也存在批评，反映出技术文章在传达信息时需要更加明确以帮助读者快速评估其价值。

43954858.article_content:
A Rust API Inspired by Python, Powered by Serde
May 7, 2025
rust
python
api
design
Years ago, I worked on reimplementing
1
some Python code in Rust (
yet again
),
and this time I needed to adapt Python’s dynamic capabilities (aka
__getattr__
) to the strict and compiled world of Rust.
After some deliberation, and armed with the
serde
(de)serialization crate, I set out to do just that.
So if you ever wondered what tricks Rust can learn from Python, and if
serde
can be used for reflection (please go along with me here), then the answer is very much yes!
Let me show you how, and also why.
Note: I’ll try to keep this somewhat approachable to Python programmers with only passing experience in Rust, it’ll be fun.
🦀🐍
A Python Inspiration
Using Python (on Windows), there’s a
magical package
that can be used to get all sorts of information about the system.
Without going into too much detail, it boils down to this: Say you want to list all the installed
physical fans
. You can do that using the following code:
import
wmi
c
=
wmi
.
WMI
()
for
fan
in
c
.
Win32_Fan
():
if
fan
.
ActiveCooling
:
print
(
f
"Fan `
{
fan
.
Name
}
` is running at
{
fan
.
DesiredSpeed
}
RPM"
)
This uses a couple of clever
__getattr__
implementations, and ends up running this equivalent code behind the scenes:
for
fan
in
c
.
query
(
"SELECT * FROM Win32_Fan"
):
if
fan
.
wmi_property
(
"ActiveCooling"
)
.
value
is
True
:
print
(
f
"Fan `
{
fan
.
wmi_property
(
'Name'
)
.
value
}
` is running at
{
fan
.
wmi_property
(
'DesiredSpeed'
)
.
value
}
RPM"
)
(The
wmi_property
method returns another object which holds the final value as well as its type.)
Putting aside
what
WMI
even is
, this is the kind of thing Python is extraordinarily good at:
A clear, concise, and intuitive interface abstracting over a complex and gnarly implementation.
In Python, you need but override a few magic methods to implement this, but Rust is a completely different beast.
What can we do if we want to create a Rust crate that provides a nice API to users, similar to the one above?
What We Are Abstracting Over
It’ll help to start by expressing the “raw” API in pure Rust. It’s raw in the sense that we can use it to get the
raw data
from the system, but nothing more.
We have two types: the
Value
type that can hold different types of values,
and the
Object
type that provides access to named attributes (which are themselves
Value
instances).
We end up with something like this (the full code is available
on GitHub
):
mod
raw_api
{
pub
struct
Object
{
..
}
pub
enum
Value
{
Bool
(
bool
),
I1
(
i8
),
// ..
UI8
(
u64
),
String
(
String
),
Object
(
Object
),
}
impl
Object
{
pub
fn
get_attr
(
&
self
,
name:
&
str
)
->
Value
{
..
}
}
pub
fn
query
(
query:
&
str
)
->
Vec
<
Object
>
{
..
}
}
Simple, but rather painful for the user to work with:
let
res
=
raw_api::query
(
"SELECT * FROM Win32_Fan"
);
for
obj
in
res
{
if
obj
.
get_attr
(
"ActiveCooling"
)
==
Value::Bool
(
true
)
{
if
let
Value::
String
(
name
)
=
obj
.
get_attr
(
"Name"
)
{
if
let
Value::
UI8
(
speed
)
=
obj
.
get_attr
(
"DesiredSpeed"
)
{
println!
(
"Fan `
{name}
` is running at
{speed}
RPM"
);
}
}
}
}
Since any field can be of any type, the user must manually check (either with
match
or, as we did, with
if let
)
what variant of the
Value
enum they got every time they interact with it.
This is especially cumbersome when one wants to query many different types of objects (
Win32_Battery
🔋,
Win32_UserAccount
💁,
Win32_Printer
🖨️, …).
Note: this is a simplification of the
underlying API
we have to use,
but it’s close enough that we can design our higher level API based on it. You can check the
wmi-rs
crate
source code for the full details.
A Possible Design
Inspired by the Pythonic API, what if instead we could do something like this:
// 1. The user defines a custom struct for the type of objects to query.
struct
Fan
{
name:
String
,
active_cooling:
bool
,
desired_speed:
u64
,
}
// 2. Specify that `query` should to return instances of `Fan`.
let
res:
Vec
<
Fan
>
=
api::query
();
// 3. Profit.
for
fan
in
res
{
if
fan
.
active_cooling
{
println!
(
"Fan `
{}
` is running at
{}
RPM"
,
fan
.
name
,
fan
.
desired_speed
);
}
}
Much nicer!
One of the distinct features of Rust is that
generic return types
can change the behavior of a function
(with
.collect()
being the most famous example of this), so how can we implement something like this?
Imagine we went ahead and updated
query
to accept some generic type
T
.
What trait can we use to constrain
T
so we can implement the function?
fn
query
<
T
>
()
->
Vec
<
T
>
where
T:
???
{
???
}
The standard library offers
any::type_name
which could (not really) help us to build the
SELECT
query,
but without resorting to
violence
, we seem to be on our own.
Crawl Before You Can Walk
Let’s start with a relatively simple solution: Let’s
define a new trait
that:
Provides the name of the object to query.
Handles the construction of e.g.
Fan
s from
Object
s.

Hello!
I've recently been working on the pathfinding for NPCs in my game, which is something I've been looking forward to for a while now since it's a nice chunky problem to solve. I thought I'd write up this post about how I went about it all.
I had a few extra requirements of my pathfinding, due to how my game plays:
Must deal with a dynamic physical environment (objects can move freely and are destructible)
Have paths that prefer to keep their distance from objects but still get close when needed
Allow for wrapping around the borders of the game area (Asteroids style)
General Approach
My first thought was that I wanted detailed paths so that they could thread through messy arrangements of objects quite easily. This would mean a longer search time, so the simple choice of search algorithm is A*. And since I need to query the world for each node to see whether it's blocked, I thought I'd use space partitioning with the queries to cut down on the number required for each path.
I ended up sticking to this plan, and figuring out the more detailed stuff along the way.
Space Partitioned Queries
I built a space partitioning tree where each node covers a specific area of the game, and then each of that node's children covers a specific area of their parent's area (with the tree's root covering the whole game area). I do this to a depth of 6 and then the leaf nodes effectively make up the navigation grid for path finding.
Now when I check if a node is blocked it will first check its parent. If its parent is not blocked, then none of its children are blocked. If the parent is blocked, then the child node needs to run its own query to see whether its own area is blocked. This allows us to know whether large areas of the game are not blocked in very few queries, which is useful because these queries are expensive.
A* Search
The actual search is a pretty standard A* search. Each node has 8 neighbours, with nodes on the edge having wrapped neighbours, which are cached along with their traversal cost for faster lookup.
Environment Changing in Real Time
Because objects can move around in the game world and even have chunks of them destroyed, this algorithm needed to be able to update in real time. The asteroid that wasn't blocking the path a second ago might have moved, and the asteroid that was blocking the path might have been blown up!
My simple solution for this was to allow the algorithm to cache whether each node it checked was blocked, but then invalidate that cache every so often (currently every 500ms is working nicely). This allows time to build up a picture of the world and let one path finding request use information from a previous request, but also forces the algorithm to keep up to date on the current state of the world.
Ideally we wouldn't invalidate the whole cache since there will be sections of the game world where nothing has moved, but realistically this is a simple approach that works well enough. Saying that, I do have a plan on how to do this should it be necessary.
Here you can see the spreading out and being updated in real time. Each blue square represents an unblocked node, and the colour of the pixel in the node represents proximity to the nearest object.
Natural Paths
The shortest path doesn't usually look natural, or safe for that matter, so I wanted the algorithm to prefer paths that are further away from objects but still be able to get close when necessary (threading through a small gap, for example).
So for each pathfinding request a preferred distance from objects is provided, which is then used to give each node a proximity rating. This proximity rating is used when determining the traversal cost to a node, so nodes that are closer to objects are simply more expensive when running the search.
Currently the proximity rating has an exponential effect, so the path really tries to avoid being super close to things, but doesn't mind being a little close if it has to.
Here you can see the path keeping its distance from objects until its forced to get closer and in between them. You can also see the space partitioning better here, with the larger blue squares representing areas that only required a single query.
Wrapped Paths
Because the game area allows for Asteroids-like wrapping, I wanted the pathfinding to account for this too. NPCs not having the same kind of mobility as the player is a bit jarring, plus it made the problem a little more fun to solve. :)
Wrapped paths mean that every navigation node actually has the same number of neighbours, which is an interesting and maybe uncommon property (pathfinding on a 3d globe probably has the same property).

data.title: My Engineering Craft Regressed
data.author: OsrsNeedsf2P
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己大学毕业后，投身开源项目并获得用户认可，但在求职过程中发现招聘方并不重视这些实际项目。在申请600多份工作后，仅获得3个offer，最终选择了一家待遇一般但尊重他的公司。之后，作者继续在开源项目上投入大量时间，但这些努力并未带来预期的高薪工作。为了提高收入，作者开始专注于Leetcode刷题，最终获得了5倍薪资增长，尽管技能有所退步，却受到多家公司青睐。作者对开源世界的热情逐渐冷却，计划赚够钱后退休，希望那时的开源社区仍保持原样。

5 years ago when I graduated University, I had a whole host of open source projects under my belt. I put my heart and soul into them - for thousands of hours. And users loved them. I still remember some of the faceless users whose messages gave me a smile.
When I went into the job market - which was much better back then - I had some incorrect assumption that recruiters would care about this work. Or at least technically inclined companies. Or at the very least, companies
I
would want to work for would care about this.
But that never happened. My Indeed profile shows I applied to over 600 jobs back then. With 3 offers, I accepted the only one that didn’t treat me like a baby, and had a great time working for that company.
During the day, I worked 8-9 hours for this startup, and until late at night I continued my open source contributions. Surely, they would take me somewhere.
I hopped to another startup and oversaw major projects - for pitiful pay - but enjoyed it. My skillset had never been so strong, and my impact was measurably through the roof. Surely if I kept this up, I would land a high paying gig anytime soon.
But of course, that didn’t happen. Waking up at 6am to make some commits, reading documentation on the subway, and coding to dubstep at night wasn’t getting me anywhere. But I was happy.
Eventually I came to face the music - Nobody gives a crap about real projects. The people who knew my value weren’t the people who could pay me. I peeled back, and started grinding Leetcode instead.
My projects slowed to a crawl. The communities slowly got demotivated. It was sad to turn my back to, but it got me a 5x salary bump.
When I joined, I was treated like a baby for having “4 years of industry experience”. Whatever. I did work here and there, and apparently my impact exceeded expectations.
But what about my skillset? Despite significantly regressing, now my email is filled with recruiters begging me to come to be “Amazon SDE II”, “Tech lead at YC startup X”, “Part time job paying 150-290$/hr”. Pathetic. I was so much better (and happier) before, yet I’m only seen when I do the fake crap like update my LinkedIn to celebrate 1 year at $FAANG.
I’ll collect some money and retire in a couple years. Hopefully the open source world stays the same until then.

• ZephyrBlu指出，技能和市场需求之间的不对等现象。即使技能退步，一些人仍因其名声而更受欢迎，这种现象让人感觉荒谬。

• _factor强调，招聘过程中非技术性招聘人员对候选人的误判问题。他们依赖关键词和行业术语筛选简历，导致一些真正有才华的开发人员因为不善表达而被忽视。

• notepad0x90建议，开发人员应该在工作之外从事自己热爱的项目，但不要为了找工作或美化简历而做，而是为了乐趣。

• ChrisMarshallNY分享了自己的经验，他长期从事个人项目，尽管这些项目不为雇主所知或关心，但他从中获得了乐趣和成就感。

• franciscop表达了对个人项目热情的转变，认为生活中还有其他值得追求的事情，未来可能会探索新的兴趣爱好。

• j3s对帖子的语气表示不满，质疑是否应该对一个高薪但无法兼顾 passion 项目的人感到同情。

• butterlettuce调侃自己只需 grind leetcode，而无需在意项目，反映出对技术面试准备的无奈。

• taurath讨论了“精英体制神话”问题，指出在软件行业中，社交信号和文凭等其他技能标志往往比实际技能更重要。他强调建立关系对职业发展的重要性。

• hnthrow90348765认为，在大公司工作可能会让人重新发现软件开发的内在价值，尽管初期感觉这份工作只是赚钱的工具。

• sorokod指出，过度需要他人肯定是一种心理负担。

• camcil简单总结，报酬基于提供的商业价值，不同组织可能采用不同的评估方式。

• ChrisArchitect提到一个技术社区平台Lemmy是否适合用于个人博客托管的问题，反映出对技术工具用途的探讨。

data.title: California sent residents' personal health data to LinkedIn
data.author: anticorporate
data.article_summary: 《The Markup》调查发现，加州平价医疗法案（Affordable Care Act）的健康保险网站coveredca.com向LinkedIn传输敏感数据。当用户填写有关是否失明、怀孕、使用多种处方药等问题时，网站上的跟踪器会将这些信息发送给LinkedIn，甚至包括是否为跨性别者或家暴受害者。该行为是在一个广告活动中进行的，目前这些跟踪器已被移除。Covered California表示正在审查数据安全和隐私协议，确保不会非法共享用户信息。此事件引发了对隐私违规的担忧，有专家指出这种做法侵犯了用户隐私。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Covered California向LinkedIn等平台泄露敏感健康信息的问题，以及相关数据追踪和隐私保护的争议。

不同观点：
• [kordlessagain] 认为，Covered California泄露敏感健康信息的问题反映了更广泛的行业问题，即原本用于护理的基础设施被用于广告行为 targeting。作者质疑科技公司和AI系统背后的动机，认为这些行为并非出于智慧，而是出于权力集中和恐惧落后。
• [vharuck] 认为，Covered California使用60多个追踪器是故意为之，而非简单的失误。他对为什么一个仅处理健康保险的独立机构需要如此多的追踪器表示疑惑，并指出这种行为明显不妥。
• [bensonn] 强调，称这些数据为“泄露”并不准确，因为添加LinkedIn追踪代码是故意行为，追踪器按设计执行了其功能。他指出，这是Covered California的选择，而非意外。
• [neilv] 分享了个人经历，LinkedIn根据其浏览历史展示了相关广告，质疑是否有人将私人医疗信息提供给了LinkedIn。
• [oaththrowaway] 质疑为什么一个州级机构需要进行广告追踪，认为这可能是为了资金需求。
• [1024core] 直接指出这种行为可能违反HIPAA法案，并对此表示惊讶。
• [knowitnone] 认为，加州的调查可能会偏袒自己，且指出LinkedIn与Microsoft的关系。
• [blindriver] 询问定期清除cookies是否能防止长期追踪。
• [goldchainposse] 解释说，许多公司主动将数据提供给大科技公司，而非出售数据，科技公司利用这些数据进行广告投放。
• [treebeard901] 详细描述了医疗记录的复杂性和潜在的滥用问题，指出医疗信息的共享和不透明性问题严重。
• [barbazoo] 试图澄清，是否需要用户故意点击广告才能让LinkedIn获取敏感信息。
• [dzdt] 指出，根据Covered California的隐私政策，这种数据共享行为可能违反HIPAA法案，并引用了相关文件支持其观点。
• [actionfromafar] 提到联邦政府也曾将居民的健康数据发送给xAI，认为当前问题不仅限于州级。
• [rob_c] 批评州级机构在处理公共数据和敏感信息方面的无能，建议相关负责人辞职。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Covered California是否故意泄露敏感信息，以及这种行为是否违反相关隐私保护法律如HIPAA。
• 讨论中还涉及科技公司和AI系统在数据收集和广告投放中的角色和动机。
• 有人质疑政府机构为何需要进行广告追踪，是否出于资金需求。
• 医疗记录的共享和不透明性问题也被详细讨论，反映出对整个医疗信息系统的广泛担忧。

The Markup, now a part of CalMatters, uses investigative reporting, data analysis, and software engineering to challenge technology to serve the public good. Sign up for

The website that lets Californians shop for health insurance under the Affordable Care Act, coveredca.com, has been sending sensitive data to  LinkedIn, forensic testing by The Markup has revealed.
As visitors filled out forms on the website, trackers on the same pages told LinkedIn their answers to questions about whether they were blind, pregnant, or used a high number of prescription medications. The trackers also monitored whether the visitors said they were transgender or possible victims of domestic abuse.
See our data here
Github
Covered California, the organization that operates the website, removed the trackers as The Markup and CalMatters reported this article. The organization said they were removed “due to a marketing agency transition” in early April.
In a statement, Kelly Donohue, a spokesperson for the agency, confirmed that data was sent to LinkedIn as part of an advertising campaign. Since  being informed of the tracking, “all active advertising-related tags across our website have been turned off out of an abundance of caution,” she added.
“Covered California has initiated a review of our websites and information security and privacy protocols to ensure that no analytics tools are impermissibly sharing sensitive consumer information,” Donohue said, adding that they would “share additional findings as they become available, taking any necessary steps to safeguard the security and privacy of consumer data.”
When an individual indicated they were pregnant, the information was sent to LinkedIn via the Insight Tag.
Credit:
Visitors who filled out health information on the site may have had their data tracked for more than a year, according to Donohue, who said the LinkedIn campaign began in February 2024.

Impact

Covered California
released a statement
saying it was “reviewing the nature and extent of sensitive consumer data and information that was inadvertently shared with LinkedIn.”
May 1, 2025:
Rep. Kevin Kiley, a Republican representing inland California areas, called the sharing of sensitive data with LinkedIn "
incredibly disturbing
" and
asked the Department of Health and Human Services to investigate
whether it violated privacy regulations in the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act.
Read more
The Markup observed the trackers directly in February and March of this year. It confirmed most ad trackers, including the Meta “pixel” tracker, as well as all third-party cookies, have been removed from the site as of April 21.
Since 2014, more than 50 million Americans have
signed up
for health insurance through state exchanges like Covered California. They were set up under the
Affordable Care Act
, signed into law by President Barack Obama 15 years ago. States can either operate their exchange websites in partnership with the federal government or independently,
as California does
.
Covered California operates as an independent entity within the state government. Its
board
is appointed by the governor and Legislature.
In March,
Covered California announced
that, after four years of increasing enrollment, a record of nearly 2 million people were covered by health insurance through the program. In all, the organization said, about one in six Californians were at one point enrolled through Covered California. Between 2014 and 2023, the uninsured rate fell from 17.2% to 6.4%, according to the organization, the largest drop of any state during that time period. This
coincided with a series of eligibility
expansions to
Medi-Cal
, the state’s health insurance program for lower-income households.
Report Deeply and Fix Things
Because it turns out moving fast and breaking things broke some super important things.
Give Now
Experts expressed alarm at the idea that those millions of people could have had sensitive health data sent to a private company without their knowledge or consent. Sara Geoghegan, senior counsel at the Electronic Privacy Information Center, said it was “concerning and invasive” for a health insurance website to be sending data that was “wholly irrelevant” to the uses of a for-profit company like LinkedIn.
“It’s unfortunate,” she said, “because people don’t expect that their health information will be collected and used in this way.”

Blacklight
, an automated tool developed by The Markup for auditing website trackers.

data.title: Forget IPs: using cryptography to verify bot and agent traffic
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在AI代理流量增加的背景下，如何区分合法爬虫和恶意机器人。传统上，Cloudflare依靠用户代理头和IP地址验证爬虫身份，但这些方法存在易被伪造和不准确的问题。为了解决这一问题，文章提出了两种新的认证机制——HTTP消息签名和请求mTLS，以帮助友好机器人验证自身身份。

现有方法的问题包括：用户代理头易被伪造，IP地址共享和变化频繁，以及每个网站单独共享秘密（如Bearer token）不切实际。新机制利用加密技术，使机器人开发者能够对其服务发出的请求进行加密签名，从而使像Cloudflare这样的反向代理能够验证请求来源，帮助网站所有者更好地管理流量。

HTTP消息签名是一种标准化的请求加密认证方式，使来源能够确认发送者身份。请求mTLS则通过双向TLS验证实现更强的安全性。文章还邀请开发者参与其封闭测试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对恶意流量和爬虫活动，以及在技术上可能的解决方案和隐私问题。

不同观点：
• Lockhead认为，虽然该方法可以帮助检测合法的机器人，但仍然难以区分真实用户和恶意流量。合法的机器人数量较少且行为透明，容易识别，但要实现该方法的实际应用，用户需要参与，这会引发隐私问题。

• Ok123456建议在SMTP中引入工作量证明扩展，使得小型SMTP中继可以通过解决计算问题来增加邮件投递的机会，且问题的难度可以与发送者的声誉成反比。

• Unsolved73对当前使用 obscure RFC 而非更普遍的 JSON Web Tokens（JWTs）的HTTP签名方法提出质疑，认为这可能导致有趣的漏洞。

• PaulHoule指出，AI训练和推理都是驱动机器人活动的重要因素。尤其是AI推理可以通过自动生成爬虫代码和执行复杂的工作流来增加爬虫的使用，但这些活动可能因验证码等问题而中断。

• Nubinetwork反对对HTTP请求进行复杂分析，认为这会增加服务器负担，不利于运行网站。

• Dboreham猜测，这种技术讨论的潜台词可能是为爬虫流量引入收费。

• Senectus1分享了一个自托管的类似解决方案，并对其表示赞赏。

• Superkuh批评依赖中心化的证书机构和短寿命密钥的技术方案，认为这会提高人类参与网络的难度，最终可能导致网络的封闭化。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于技术实现的复杂性、隐私问题以及对用户和开发者的影响。
- 讨论中涉及的具体技术包括工作量证明、HTTP签名、SMTP扩展、自托管解决方案等。
- 部分评论者关注爬虫活动对网络资源的消耗，以及如何有效限制恶意流量而不影响合法机器人。
- 另一个值得注意的方面是对网络基础设施集中化的担忧，以及对未来网络开放性的潜在影响。

43994779.article_content:
Forget IPs: using cryptography to verify bot and agent traffic
2025-05-15
Thibault Meunier
Mari Galicer
10 min read
With the rise of traffic from AI agents, whatâs considered a bot is no longer clear-cut. There are some clearly malicious bots, like ones that DoS your site or do credential stuffing, and ones that most site owners do want to interact with their site, like the bot that indexes your site for a search engine, or ones that fetch RSS feeds.Â Â Â Â Â Â
Historically, Cloudflare has relied on two main signals to verify legitimate web crawlers from other types of automated traffic: user agent headers and IP addresses. The
User-Agent
header
allows bot developers to identify themselves, i.e.
MyBotCrawler/1.1
. However, user agent headers alone are easily spoofed and are therefore insufficient for reliable identification. To address this, user agent checks are often supplemented with
IP address validation
, the inspection of published IP address ranges to confirm a crawler's authenticity. However, the logic around IP address ranges representing a product or group of users is brittle â connections from the crawling service might be shared by multiple users, such as in the case of
privacy proxies
and VPNs, and these ranges, often maintained by cloud providers, change over time.
Cloudflare will always try to block malicious bots, but we think our role here is to also provide an affirmative mechanism to authenticate desirable bot traffic. By using well-established cryptography techniques, weâre proposing a better mechanism for legitimate agents and bots to declare who they are, and provide a clearer signal for site owners to decide what traffic to permit.Â
Today, weâre introducing two proposals â HTTP message signatures and request mTLS â for
friendly bots
to authenticate themselves, and for customer origins to identify them.
In this blog post, weâll share how these authentication mechanisms work, how we implemented them, and how you can participate in our closed beta.
Existing bot verification mechanisms are brokenÂ
Historically, if youâve worked on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or any other agent, youâve had several options to identify your HTTP traffic to other services:Â
You define a
user agent
, an HTTP header described in
RFC 9110
. The problem here is that this header is easily spoofable and thereâs not a clear way for agents to identify themselves as semi-automated browsers â agents often use the Chrome user agent for this very reason, which is discouraged. The RFC
states
:
âIf a user agent masquerades as a different user agent, recipients can assume that the user intentionally desires to see responses tailored for that identified user agent, even if they might not work as well for the actual user agent being used.â
Â
You publish your IP address range(s). This has limitations because the same IP address might be shared by multiple users or multiple services within the same company, or even by multiple companies when hosting infrastructure is shared (like Cloudflare Workers, for example). In addition, IP addresses are prone to change as underlying infrastructure changes, leading services to use ad-hoc sharing mechanisms like
CIDR lists
.Â
You go to every website and share a secret, like a
Bearer
token. This is impractical at scale because it requires developers to maintain separate tokens for each website their bot will visit.
We can do better! Instead of these arduous methods, weâre proposing that developers of bots and agents cryptographically sign requests originating from their service. When protecting origins, reverse proxies such as Cloudflare can then validate those signatures to confidently identify the request source on behalf of site owners, allowing them to take action as they see fit.Â
A typical system has three actors:
User: the entity that wants to perform some actions on the web. This may be a human, an automated program, or anything taking action to retrieve information from the web.
Agent: an orchestrated browser or software program. For example, Chrome on your computer, or OpenAIâs
Operator
with ChatGPT. Agents can interact with the web according to web standards (HTML rendering, JavaScript, subrequests, etc.).
Origin: the website hosting a resource. The user wants to access it through the browser. This is Cloudflare when your website is using our services, and itâs your own server(s) when exposed directly to the Internet.
In the next section, weâll dive into HTTP Message Signatures and request mTLS, two mechanisms a browser agent may implement to sign outgoing requests, with different levels of ease for an origin to adopt.Â
Introducing HTTP Message Signatures
HTTP Message Signatures
is a standard that defines the cryptographic authentication of a request sender. Itâs essentially a cryptographically sound way to say, âhey, itâs me!â. Itâs not the only way that developers can sign requests from their infrastructure â for example, AWS has used
S
