The Chuwi MiniBook X N150
The netbook era has come and gone, but I am one of the many people who miss small form factor laptops (12” or smaller), and I’ve found it somewhat frustrating that they’ve been nowhere to be found in mainstream offerings.
But one day I was doing a tally of Intel N-series devices that would be interesting prospects for a few scenarios and stumbled upon the Chuwi
MiniBook X N150
, which I was profoundly intrigued by and just
had
to try out:
The MiniBook X N150
And that is exactly what I have been doing for a few weeks now. In fact, I’ve been using it as a daily driver for both work and personal stuff, and this post is very much a hands-on review of what it’s been like so far.
Disclaimer:
Chuwi
sent me a review sample of the
MiniBook X 150
free of charge (for which I thank them), and as usual this article follows
my review policy
.
But since the picture above might not give you a good notion of scale, here it is besides my MacBook:
Sorry, I was out of bananas
Design
First impressions were pretty great: the
MiniBook
(as I will refer to it from here on) has a metallic grey, branding-free aluminum outer shell (the keyboard frame and sides are plastic) that is heavily reminiscent of a MacBook (even down to the inset in front of the trackpad), a nice clear screen with very sturdy hinges that are reminiscent of my
Lenovo X1 Yoga
, and relatively thin bezels with a discrete logo just below the screen.
The MacBook-like theme is reinforced by the minimal set of USB-C ports that, again, feels very familiar, but it also has hints of Lenovo-style design:
The X, a MacBook 13", a Lenovo X1 Yoga and a modern MacBook Pro
Regardless of influence, it’s a great blend of minimalism and functionality, and if you don’t have a visual reference for size, you would be excused for thinking it is a full-blown high-end laptop.
Hardware
The
MiniBook
has gone through a few hardware iterations, but the current incarnation is based on the Intel Twin Lake
N150
and has the following system specs:
4 cores that can burst up to 3.6GHz (and go as low as 700MHz for power saving)
1920x1200 10” display run by Intel graphics with 24 EUs
12GB LPDDR5 RAM
512GB NVMe SSD
2 USB-C ports
1 audio combo jack
The
N150
also has a few of the new Intel chipset features for neural and image processing, although there is no software that actually takes advantage of those as far as I know (I did have a go at Intel’s
SYCL
, but couldn’t get it to work–see below).
Ports
You get a mic/headphone combo jack on the left (thank goodness) and two USB-C ports on the right, one of which supports USB PD and (oh luxury of luxuries) actually has a charging light, unlike my MacBook Pro.
Close-up of the ports on either side
Both ports support display output, and I had zero issues connecting the
MiniBook
to my LG monitors for both display and power or using a small portable monitor (more on that later).
But, of course, the biggest feature of a small laptop like this is the screen (pun intended).
Screen
The
MiniBook
has a nice, glossy (but thankfully not overly reflective) 1920x1200 touch screen with a 16:10 aspect ratio that I’ve found comfortable to use despite its size. The interesting side effect of this combination of size and resolution is that you get nearly twice the usual density of an FHD panel, which in turn means that text rendering is very sharp, making it look very much like a top-tier HIDPI display.
Since I spend most of my time reading or crafting text, this is the part I appreciate the most, and the extra vertical 120 pixels come in handy for toolbars of various kinds.
The panel backlight is not among the brightest I’ve used, but it’s strong enough for it to be usable in fairly bright situations, like drafting this post in a bright sunlit room or the back of an Uber in sunny Portuguese weather (yes, that actually happened).
On the flip side, I typically kept the backlight at under 50% most of the time I used the machine during the evenings–although of course your mileage and needs may vary:
Another size comparison
Color reproduction is good–certainly better than my
Lenovo Ideapad Flex 5
; I have a habit of switching wallpapers daily, and although I haven’t made any scientific testing, the few photos I’ve seen and tweaked looked quite nice.
You can tent the display and even use the machine in portrait mode like a tablet–in fact, the display reports itself as being 1200x1920 when booting Linux, so “normal” use is actually rotated (more details below).
In “tablet” mode (which in Windows disables the keyboard) the
MiniBook
works OK as a somewhat thick tablet, although when playing with it in that way I was reminded that the panel does not have pen input.

data.title: Physicists snap the first images of "free-range" atoms
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: MIT物理学家首次成功拍摄到自由运动的单个原子图像，揭示了以前仅在理论上预测的量子现象。他们使用了一种新技术，先让原子云自由交互，然后通过光晶格将原子瞬间冻结，再用激光照亮这些原子，生成其位置图像。该技术帮助科学家直接观察到玻色子聚集形成波的现象，以及费米子在自由空间中配对的机制，这是超导性的关键。研究成果发表在《Physical Review Letters》上，标志着在实时可视化量子现象方面取得了重要进展。其他团队也使用了类似技术，进一步验证了这些发现。

MIT physicists have captured the first images of individual atoms freely interacting in space. The pictures reveal correlations among the “free-range” particles that until now were predicted but never directly observed. Their findings,
appearing today in the journal
Physical Review Letters
, will help scientists visualize never-before-seen quantum phenomena in real space.
The images were taken using a technique developed by the team that first allows a cloud of atoms to move and interact freely. The researchers then turn on a lattice of light that briefly freezes the atoms in their tracks, and apply finely tuned lasers to quickly illuminate the suspended atoms, creating a picture of their positions before the atoms naturally dissipate.
The physicists applied the technique to visualize clouds of different types of atoms, and snapped a number of imaging firsts. The researchers directly observed atoms known as “bosons,” which bunched up in a quantum phenomenon to form a wave. They also captured atoms known as “fermions” in the act of pairing up in free space — a key mechanism that enables superconductivity.
“We are able to see single atoms in these interesting clouds of atoms and what they are doing in relation to each other, which is beautiful,” says Martin Zwierlein, the Thomas A. Frank Professor of Physics at MIT.
In the same journal issue, two other groups report using similar imaging techniques, including a team led by Nobel laureate Wolfgang Ketterle, the John D. MacArthur Professor of Physics at MIT. Ketterle’s group visualized enhanced pair correlations among bosons, while the other group, from École Normale Supérieure in Paris, led by Tarik Yefsah, imaged a cloud of noninteracting fermions.
The study by Zwierlein and his colleagues is co-authored by MIT graduate students Ruixiao Yao, Sungjae Chi, and Mingxuan Wang, and MIT assistant professor of physics Richard Fletcher.
Inside the cloud
A single atom is about one-tenth of a nanometer in diameter, which is one-millionth of the thickness of a strand of human hair. Unlike hair, atoms behave and interact according to the rules of quantum mechanics; it is their quantum nature that makes atoms difficult to understand. For example, we cannot simultaneously know precisely where an atom is and how fast it is moving.
Scientists can apply various methods to image individual atoms, including absorption imaging, where laser light shines onto the atom cloud and casts its shadow onto a camera screen.

data.title: Most Americans don't earn enough to afford basic costs of living
data.author: ripe

44000562.article_content:
Inflation rate hits lowest level since 2021
Annual inflation rate in April hits lowest level since 2021, but still higher than Fed's goal
03:05
The gap between what Americans earn and how much they need to bring in to achieve a basic standard of living is growing, according to a new
report
.
The analysis, from the Ludwig Institute for Shared Economic Prosperity (LISEP), looks beyond whether people can afford daily necessities like food and shelter to consider whether they have the means to pay for things like the technology tools necessary for work, higher education, and health and child care costs.
In tracking costs associated with what the group calls a "basket of American dream essentials," LISEP says its Minimal Quality of Life index provides a truer picture of how Americans are faring than standard economic data, such as the nation's gross domestic product and jobless rate. The index captures the annual change in the typical costs facing low- and moderate-income households who are looking to maintain a basic quality of life.
"We analyze these components not just in terms of financial figures but as crucial elements that shape a family's capability to achieve a desirable standard of living," the group explains in a
paper
describing its approach.
The findings? For the bottom 60% of U.S. households, a "minimal quality of life" is out of reach, according to the group, a research organization focused on improving lower earners' economic well-being.
"The middle class has been declining — we just haven't recognized it fully," LISEP Chairman Gene Ludwig told CBS MoneyWatch. "It's really dangerous because it's the kind of thing that leads to social unrest, and it's not fair. The American dream is not that it's given to you — it's that if you work hard, you have a chance to get ahead and achieve the things in life that you want to achieve. It's not living in a tent, not having to steal."
The Ludwig Institute also says that the nation's official
unemployment rate of 4.2%
greatly understates the level of economic distress around the U.S. Factoring in workers who are stuck in poverty-wage jobs and people who are unable to find full-time employment, the U.S. jobless rate now tops 24%, according to LISEP, which defines these groups as "functionally unemployed."
Peering beneath the surface
By those standards, the lowest-earning Americans around the U.S. are falling well short, according to LISEP. These households, which in 2023 earned an average of $38,000 per year, would need to make $67,000 to afford the items the group tracks as part of its index, which also includes professional clothing and basic leisure activities.
"Traditional headline economic indicators like GDP and unemployment tell us the economy is thriving, but they don't reflect the lived reality of most Americans," Ludwig said in a statement. "Americans are working harder than ever, fueling our economic growth, but the benefits of that hard work are not being distributed in a way that supports upward mobility for too many middle- and low-income Americans."
From 2001 to 2023, the cost of affording what amounts to a basic level of economic security doubled, according to LISEP's analysis. Housing and health care costs surged, while the amount of savings required to attend an in-state, public university soared 122%.
Meanwhile, median earnings for the bottom 60% of income earners fell 4% over that span when adjusting for the cost of goods tracked by the group's index, according to LISEP. Income growth for these households has also lagged, rising 0.37% per year during the same period — less than half as much as for the top 40% of earners, the group found.
The gap between how much low-income families earn and how much they need to afford a minimum cost of living is expected to keep widening, Ludwig told CBS MoneyWatch.
"Unfortunately, it is growing because the items that go into the basket of goods and services that make the minimal quality of life are inflating at a higher rate than wages are inflating," he said.

data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了OpenAI联合创始人兼首席科学家Ilya Sutskever在2023年对人工智能通用智能（AGI）即将到来的焦虑和思考。尽管OpenAI在AI领域取得了巨大成功，Sutskever却对AGI可能带来的文明变革感到担忧。他开始将一半的时间用于AI安全研究，并提出为应对AGI发布后的混乱建造庇护所（bunker）的计划。这种担忧在公司内部并非孤例，CEO Sam Altman也曾公开表示AGI可能带来灭绝风险。然而，OpenAI同时面临着商业扩展的压力，导致其最初的非营利理想逐渐被侵蚀。Sutskever与公司高层的理念冲突在2023年底达到顶峰，显示出OpenAI在追求AGI发展与安全之间的矛盾。

Alex Reisner
I
n the summer of 2023
, Ilya Sutskever, a co-founder and the chief scientist of OpenAI, was meeting with a group of new researchers at the company. By all traditional metrics, Sutskever should have felt invincible: He was the brain behind the large language models that helped build ChatGPT, then the fastest-growing app in history; his company’s valuation had skyrocketed; and OpenAI was the unrivaled leader of the industry believed to power the future of Silicon Valley. But the chief scientist seemed to be at war with himself.
Sutskever had long believed that artificial general intelligence, or AGI, was inevitable—now, as things accelerated in the generative-AI industry, he believed AGI’s arrival was
imminent
, according to Geoff Hinton, an AI pioneer who was his Ph.D. adviser and mentor, and another person familiar with Sutskever’s thinking. (Many of the sources in this piece requested anonymity in order to speak freely about OpenAI without fear of reprisal.) To people around him, Sutskever seemed consumed by thoughts of this impending civilizational transformation. What would the world look like when a supreme AGI emerged and surpassed humanity? And what responsibility did OpenAI have to ensure an end state of extraordinary prosperity, not extraordinary suffering?
By then, Sutskever, who had previously dedicated most of his time to advancing AI capabilities, had started to focus half of his time on AI safety. He appeared to people around him as both boomer and doomer: more excited and afraid than ever before of what was to come. That day, during the meeting with the new researchers, he laid out a plan.
“Once we all get into the bunker—” he began, according to a researcher who was present.
“I’m sorry,” the researcher interrupted, “the bunker?”
“We’re definitely going to build a bunker before we release AGI,” Sutskever replied. Such a powerful technology would surely become an object of intense desire for governments globally. The core scientists working on the technology would need to be protected. “Of course,” he added, “it’s going to be optional whether you want to get into the bunker.”
This essay has been adapted from Hao’s forthcoming book,
Empire of AI
.
Two other sources I spoke with confirmed that Sutskever commonly mentioned such a bunker. “There is a group of people—Ilya being one of them—who believe that building AGI will bring about a rapture,” the researcher told me. “Literally, a rapture.” (Sutskever declined to comment on this story.)
Sutskever’s fears about an all-powerful AI may seem extreme, but they are not altogether uncommon, nor were they particularly out of step with OpenAI’s general posture at the time. In May 2023, the company’s CEO, Sam Altman, co-signed an open letter
describing
the technology as a potential extinction risk—a narrative that has
arguably
helped OpenAI center itself and steer regulatory conversations. Yet the concerns about a coming apocalypse would also have to be balanced against OpenAI’s growing business: ChatGPT was a hit, and Altman wanted more.
When OpenAI was founded, the idea was to develop AGI for the benefit of humanity. To that end, the co-founders—who included Altman and Elon Musk—set the organization up as a nonprofit and pledged to share research with other institutions. Democratic participation in the technology’s development was a key principle, they agreed, hence the company’s name. But by the time I started
covering the company
in 2019, these ideals were eroding. OpenAI’s executives had realized that the path they wanted to take would demand extraordinary amounts of money. Both Musk and Altman tried to take over as CEO. Altman won out. Musk left the organization in early 2018 and took his money with him. To plug the hole, Altman reformulated OpenAI’s legal structure, creating a new “capped-profit” arm within the nonprofit to raise more capital.
Since then, I’ve tracked OpenAI’s evolution through interviews with more than 90 current and former employees, including executives and contractors. The company declined my repeated interview requests and questions over the course of working on my book about it, which this story is adapted from; it did not reply when I reached out one more time before the article was published. (OpenAI also has a corporate partnership with
The Atlantic
.)
OpenAI’s dueling cultures—the ambition to safely develop AGI, and the desire to grow a massive user base through new product launches—would explode toward the end of 2023. data.title: Pinta - free, open-source program for drawing and image editing
data.author: hbarka
data.article_summary: Pinta是一款免费、开源的绘图和图像编辑软件，提供直观的工具和强大的功能，适合各种水平的用户使用。它具有简化的工作流程和熟悉的界面，支持选择、裁剪、旋转、克隆、魔术棒等多种工具，适用于素描、修图、数字绘画和像素艺术等多种用途。Pinta具备实时预览和无限撤销功能，让用户可以无顾虑地进行创作和实验。软件跨平台支持Linux、Mac、Windows和*BSD，提供灵活且高效的图像编辑体验。无论是精细调整还是探索新想法，Pinta都能让过程流畅而愉快。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软是否应该停止支持MS Paint，以及替代软件的使用体验

不同观点：
• [对MS Paint被停用的不满] hbarka认为MS Paint是一个轻量级、单一用途的应用，类似于简单的厨房工具，使用方便。他质疑微软是否有必要停用MS Paint，因为该应用体积小（仅几百KB）。这反映了一些用户对经典软件被淘汰的不满，尤其是当该软件具有简单、高效的特点时。

• [替代软件的推荐] hbarka表示很高兴找到了Pinta，并认为Pinta使用起来感觉不错。这表明在MS Paint被停用后，一些用户选择了其他替代软件，并且对这些替代品感到满意，认为它们能够满足类似的需求。

补充讨论：
• [软件体积与功能的关系] hbarka提到MS Paint体积小（仅几百KB），暗示小体积软件在功能专注和资源占用上的优势。这可能是一些用户喜欢MS Paint的原因之一，他们偏好简洁、不复杂的工具。

• [用户适应新软件的能力] 评论中未直接提及争议，但潜在的讨论可能是用户对新软件的适应能力以及替代软件的学习曲线。虽然hbarka对Pinta感到满意，但其他用户可能面临寻找和适应新工具的挑战。

争议焦点：微软停用MS Paint的决定是否合理，尤其是对那些依赖简单工具的用户来说。同时，用户对替代软件的接受程度和适应能力也是一个潜在讨论点。

主要讨论点：词向量（word embeddings）及其运算的有效性和局限性

不同观点：
• **godelski** 认为词向量运算在某些情况下（如"king - man + woman = queen"）有效，但多数情况下距离定义不明确，尤其是在高维空间中（如"data + plural = number"等例子），这反映了维度灾难问题，并且这个问题尚未得到足够关注。
• **montebicyclelo** 质疑经典例子（如"king - man + woman = queen"）是否只是特例，并提出大多数词向量运算可能只会产生模糊相关的词，这表明简化的词向量算术可能存在局限性。
• **spindump8930** 赞赏工具的界面，并指出词向量运算需要一些技巧才能得到有意义的结果，比如排除查询中已有的词。同时提到词向量中的偏见问题已有研究，但未引起足够重视。

补充讨论：
• **antidnan** 和 **jumploops** 提到了类似概念的游戏（如"infinite craft"），表明词向量运算的趣味性和应用潜力，但也暗示了生成结果可能存在重复性。
• **lcnPylGDnU4H9OF** 分享了多个词向量运算的例子，有些结果有趣且合理，但也有一些令人困惑（如"map - legend = Mercator projection"）。
• **lightyrs** 和 **ale42** 展示了词向量运算的一些奇怪结果（如"life + death = mortality"、"woman + man = adult female body"），质疑这些运算在某些场景下的有效性。
• **__MatrixMan__** 提出了一个挑战，试图找到从"hammer"减去某个词而不产生包含"gun"子串的词，反映了系统生成结果的局限性。
• **grey-area** 认为系统生成结果往往是无意义的，偶尔听起来有趣，但缺乏对世界的理解和模型。
• **nxa** 提供了一些技术细节，如词定义和专有名词的处理，并表示会根据反馈改进工具。
• **anonu** 提到了类似的烦人单词游戏（如"contexto"），暗示词向量运算可能在某些应用中让人感到挫折。
• **GrantMoyer** 分享了自己之前的一个类似项目，指出得到合理的结果并不容易，支持了词向量运算的复杂性。
• **rdlw** 提出了一个技术性问题，如何找到模型中最重要的一些向量，并建议通过列出所有向量对来寻找常见但不易察觉的概念，如性别向量或语法特征向量。

争议焦点：
• 词向量运算是否仅仅依赖特例（如"king - man + woman = queen"），还是在广泛情况下有效。
• 词向量运算结果的合理性和重复性，尤其是在不同应用场景下的表现。
• 高维空间中距离定义不明确的问题及其对词向量运算的影响。
• 词向量中的偏见问题及其研究和应用中的重要性。

data.title: A server that wasn't meant to exist
data.author: jaypatelani
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者16年前参与的一次失败的IT系统改造经历。一位企业家的突然离世导致其家族企业陷入混乱，其遗孀和子女难以管理公司。作者被请来建立一个透明的IT系统，以解决信息分散和缺乏管控的问题。作者设置了基于NetBSD的服务器和多个虚拟机，实现了文件集中管理和数据存档。然而，公司内有人试图抵制并破坏新系统，尤其是已故企业家的得力助手，他企图恢复旧系统以掩盖财务问题。最终，由于业主缺乏经验和恐慌，作者被迫面对重做系统的压力，但他拒绝了这一要求，认为这是为了隐藏不正当的资金流动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：非营利组织的腐败与管理、数据备份与技术选择的重要性、组织内部问题与外部支持的必要性

不同观点：
• Protocolture 认为非营利组织中存在大量的合法贪污行为，通过法律漏洞进行资金滥用，并提到政府审计的局限性。他强调公众应当有权了解慈善机构资金使用的详细情况，而不仅仅是发现非法行为。
  
• Johnklos 关注数据备份的重要性，提到有人故意破坏数据以逃避责任的情况，并指出继承者往往会推卸责任，指责前任的管理问题。

• Duxup 补充了在企业中常见的财务管理松散问题，指出有些公司甚至在数月或数年后才发现资金异常，表明内部审计和监督的不足。

• Jagged-chisel 对故事中某人拒绝解决问题机会表示不解，认为如果得到足够的工具和权力，应该能够有效解决问题。

• BubbleRings 强调在提供技术建议时，如果对方不愿意完全采纳建议而选择错误做法，自己会选择退出，避免卷入不当操作。

• Draga79 作为作者，澄清故事中并未涉及黑社会，而是内部的信任滥用和不当行为，并表示不愿详述以保护隐私。

• Fokamul 对未雇佣咨询公司和否认黑社会参与表示怀疑，暗示可能存在隐瞒或管理不善。

• Bzmrgonz 讨论了技术细节，如操作系统选择和备份方案，建议使用现代工具如Nextcloud/Owncloud，并提出通过雇佣外部管理服务提供商来避免内部腐败问题。

补充讨论：
• Clysm 对文章的排版提出质疑，认为每句话后的换行没有必要。

• Mrweasol 和 Pak9rabid 提到类似的故事常涉及特定技术如NetBSD和PCEngines，显示出对技术背景的兴趣。

• Forinti 和 Adambuilds 分别提到意大利背景和医疗行业中数据管理不善的实例，扩展了讨论的应用场景。

• Freehorse 推测故事中某个家庭对其去世的父亲可能有很多不了解的地方，暗示家庭与组织之间的信息不对称。

争议焦点：
• 非营利组织中的贪污问题是否通过合法手段进行，以及如何有效监督和披露资金使用情况。
• 在处理技术和管理问题时，内部腐败与外部支持的平衡点在哪里。

43985971.article_content:
Yesterday I read a piece of news that brought back an important - and painful - episode from my career.
A story about trust, technology... and the kind of problems that can't always be solved.
About 16 years ago, I was contacted by an old friend. He was worried about a situation involving some mutual acquaintances.
To keep it short: an entrepreneur - administrator and owner of several companies - had died suddenly.
He was the kind of man who centralized everything, and his wife and children found themselves struggling to manage things.
One of the sons decided to cash out and leave the family business (focusing on his own career), while the others chose to stay involved in day-to-day operations.
The wife, elderly and retired for years, ended up at the helm, but she was clearly out of her depth.
The main issue was the complete lack of information flow: no digital systems of any kind were in place.
Employees had their own PCs (sometimes even personal laptops), and there was zero control over anything.
All the accounting and administrative data were scattered across individual machines, often taken home at the end of the day.
From the ownersâ perspective, all they saw was a huge cash flow coming in - yet the accounts were always in the red.
"If we keep going like this, weâll be bankrupt in just a few years", I was told.
What I could do was set up a proper IT system, structured to make data management transparent and traceable.
I planned - and got immediate approval for - the purchase of routers, switches, various networking devices and a server with several disks.
The OS of choice, as was my habit at the time, was NetBSD
. Thanks to XEN, I set up multiple VMs.
One handled the NAS duties (using Samba, so PCs could connect and store files directly there), another ran
Archivista
.
I even worked on translating Archivistaâs interface into Italian, since it wasnât yet localized, just to make it easier for users.
As usual in those days, I added a caching proxy (Squid) and a content filter (DansGuardian), to ensure proper usage.
The internet connection was very slow and often collapsed under heavy load - mostly recreational use, as logs revealed.
There was no supervision, and many people were downloading movies and such on company time.
As often happens, not everyone was happy.
One figure in particular - the late owner's former right-hand man - opposed the new system in every possible way.
According to him, none of this was necessary. But the real alarm bell had been his sudden change in lifestyle.
Heâd made purchases that didnât remotely align with his salary.
At the time, the company had no oversight and dealt with a lot of cash. It was all technically legal, especially given the nature of the business. I wonât go into detail - privacy matters.
Once everything was up and running, we trained the employees to use the new system.
Most were thrilled - finally able to work properly, with files in the right place and centralized document management.
OCR, archiving, etc. were all seen as major time-savers and a big boost in efficiency.
Some of the accounting staff remained skeptical, of course.
Since all of this was far from where I lived at the time, I went back to my life once the system was stable and everything in place.
A few quiet days passed - then one morning, my phone rang:
"Good morning, this is XYZ - I handle some technical aspects of a software suite used by the company where you've just installed everything.
We need to install our software, and I understand you set up the server. Iâll need the full server diagram and all the admin passwords".
I explained that it wasnât a Windows machine, as he assumed (without even having seen it), but NetBSD, running NetBSD and Linux VMs.
A few seconds of silence.
"I see. Then Iâll have to wipe it and install Windows. I need Windows, and I donât have time to wait for a new server - Iâll proceed tomorrow morning".
I froze. I told him that was not possible - the entire workflow now depended on that machine, and erasing it would be catastrophic.
"Iâll speak with the owners", I said, "and Iâm sure theyâll provide you with a separate server within hours".
No use. He started to backpedal.
To my (young) eyes, the goal was now obvious: that server had to disappear, and fast.
He said he would "restore the previous situation", and claimed the server couldnât remain as-is because
he
needed it.
I immediately called the owners. Sadly, due to inexperience and inability to handle the situation, they panicked.
They asked me to consider letting him do it, and then redoing the setup later, covering the cost of new hardware and my time.
I refused. I was young, but I already had this mindset: do whatâs right, even at the cost of profit.
This was clearly a maneuver to eliminate controls - the server, the centralized filesystem.
The goal was to hide the real accounting data from owners and auditors. Thousands of euros vanished every day through "transactions".
The

data.title: Sitting for a long time shrinks your brain even if you exercise
data.author: codexon
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：久坐与大脑退化之间的关系，以及相关的研究方法和健康影响

不同观点：
• lwo32k认为，久坐人群由于依赖现代医学技术维持生理健康，寿命延长，但大脑退化问题未得到有效解决，导致在晚年面临认知衰退的风险。这一现象类似于将人当作实验对象进行观察。
• cko担心远程办公导致的久坐生活方式对健康的负面影响，询问如何通过调整姿势和短时运动来缓解这一问题。
• ta988提出相反的观点，认为久坐可能是认知衰退的标志，而非原因，暗示可能存在基因因素或其他风险因素。
• max_认为久坐时进行知识性活动（如读书或听播客）能提升认知，并询问除IQ测试外的其他认知测试。
• rajnathani指出研究可能存在控制变量不足的问题，如久坐者可能缺乏社交活动，而孤独与痴呆风险相关。
• plsbenice34批评媒体将研究中的“关联”误导为“因果”，强调科学报道的准确性。
• justlikereddit认为大脑体积随年龄增长自然缩小，且轻度缩小对认知的影响不大。
• ch4s3对研究中的具体数据（如每天坐13小时）提出质疑。
• actinium226对研究数据的线性回归分析、单位不明确及因果关系提出批评。
• inverted_flag好奇这一现象是否适用于年轻成年人。
• ziofill对研究中散点图的线性拟合表示怀疑。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及久坐生活方式对不同年龄段人群的影响，以及如何通过运动和认知活动缓解潜在的健康风险。
• 对研究方法和数据分析的有效性提出质疑，特别是对线性回归和因果关系的误解。
• 强调现代医学在延长生理寿命的同时，对认知健康干预的不足。
• 提出社交活动和认知刺激对大脑健康的重要性。

data.title: Ollama's new engine for multimodal models
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: Ollama推出了新的多模态模型引擎，支持如Meta Llama 4、Google Gemma 3、Qwen 2.5 VL和Mistral Small 3.1等模型。引擎具备多模态理解和推理能力，例如通过Llama 4 Scout分析图片内容并回答相关问题，支持多张图片输入及关系分析（如Gemma 3），以及文档扫描和字符识别（如Qwen 2.5 VL）。Ollama的新引擎旨在提高本地推理的可靠性和准确性，并为未来支持更多模态（如语音、图像生成、视频生成等）奠定基础。该引擎还注重模型模块化和社区贡献，以增强功能和工具支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ollama新引擎及其多模态支持的分析与争议

不同观点：
• **关于时机的讨论**：
  ◦ simonw认为Ollama选择在llama.cpp刚稳定支持视觉功能时发布新引擎，时机有些出乎意料。可能Ollama早已在开发此功能，并为了掌控自己的发展路径而选择独立。
  
• **命名混乱**：
  ◦ clpm4j指出LLM领域中以"llama"命名的项目太多，造成了一定的混淆，用户很难区分不同的项目。

• **技术实现的质疑**：

data.title: I was a Theranos whistleblower. Here's what I think Elizabeth Holmes is up to
data.author: iancmceachern
data.article_summary: 文章由Theranos举报人Tyler Shultz撰写，讨论了Elizabeth Holmes的近况及其伴侣创办的血液检测公司Haemanthus。Holmes因Theranos欺诈案正在服刑，而她的伴侣Billy Evans创立了同样专注于微量血液检测的公司Haemanthus，尽管Holmes与该公司无正式关联，但其影响无处不在。Shultz认为，Holmes最初创立Theranos并非为了改革医疗，而是追求名声与成功。她善于编织故事，操控现实，甚至利用孩子和公司来塑造形象。Shultz怀疑Haemanthus可能只是她故事的延续，而非真正创新或欺诈。Holmes出狱后可能继续塑造其“传奇”形象。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• Joshdavham认为公众可以透过一个播客系列深入了解Theranos举报人的背景，并提到其中一位主持人是Y Combinator的联合创始人，暗示Theranos事件中涉及的个人背景值得关注。
• RandallBrown提出Theranos运营了15年，且雇佣了科学家和研究人员，因此质疑该公司是否至少在某些技术上取得了一定进展，或者其技术是否有可能被用于其他商业项目，而非完全失败。
• Ipv6ipv4指出在101公路上有广告牌引导人们访问Holmes的网站，该网站宣称她“已被证明无罪”，质疑Holmes是否在试图通过某种叙事重塑自己的形象。
• Threeseed提供了一个Haemanthus正在使用的专利链接，并指出该专利未引用Theranos的任何专利，表明两者之间的联系仅基于创始人之间的个人关系，而非技术关联。
• Cosmicgadget提到不少人声称发明了“可行的Theranos”，并认为如果成功，可能来自那些起步更早且没有依赖巨额种子资金的项目，质疑Theranos的巨额融资是否合理。

• Sherdil2022引用Mahatma Gandhi的名言，暗示贪婪是Theranos事件中的一个问题，但没有具体站队或提出技术性意见，更多的是一种道德反思。

44001041.article_content:
Opinion
First Opinion
I was a Theranos whistleblower. Here’s what I think Elizabeth Holmes is up to
Her partner’s new blood-testing company, Haemanthus, looks mighty familiar
Manage alerts for this article
Email this article
Share this article
Former Theranos CEO Elizabeth Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans, who has founded a company that also touts a diagnostic blood-testing device that uses only small amounts of blood.
Philip Pacheco/Getty Images
By
Tyler Shultz
May 15, 2025
Shultz is a scientist, founder, and whistleblower best known for exposing fraud at Theranos and advocating for ethics in innovation.
I always knew Elizabeth Holmes would have a second act. But I’m shocked it’s starting while she’s still behind bars.
Elizabeth is now serving an 11-year sentence for defrauding investors in Theranos and has been
banned
from participating in federal health programs. The company was built on her claim that, at 19 years old, she had invented a device capable of running hundreds of tests from just a single drop of blood. It was a bold vision that captivated the world, and a story everyone wanted to believe —
including me
.
advertisement
Now her partner, Billy Evans, has founded a company called
Haemanthus
, which also touts a diagnostic blood-testing device that uses only small amounts of blood. While Elizabeth has no legal affiliation with the company, her fingerprints and pricks are all over it. Even the naming convention feels familiar: Instead of combining the Greek roots of therapeía and diagnosis like she did with Theranos, this time it’s haema and anthos
— Greek for “blood” and “flower.”
Tyler Shultz
STAT
Since she reported to prison about two years ago, by far the most common question people have asked me is: “Did Elizabeth start Theranos with the intention to revolutionize health care, or did she intend to commit fraud from the start?” I think the answer is neither. While I wasn’t there in the early days, I believe Elizabeth started Theranos in the pursuit of fame. She wanted to be the female Steve Jobs. She wanted to be known as the youngest self-made female billionaire, fly in private jets, advise the president, rub shoulders with Mark Zuckerberg and Elon Musk. She wanted to be on the cover of magazines. And she got what she wanted. Just a few months ago, she was on the cover of People magazine. Let me repeat: Even from prison, she’s landing on the cover of People magazine.
As the news of Haemanthus broke, I started to hear a similar question: “Do you think Haemanthus intends to revolutionize health care, or do you think it’s another fraud?” Once again — neither. I think it’s just another chapter of her narrative.
advertisement
Anyone who thought this story was over doesn’t know Elizabeth and her ability to craft a narrative. When she leaves prison, there’s no doubt she’ll manage to appear remorseful without admitting guilt. And if she’s credited with launching a company from a prison cell? That’s more legendary than the Hewlett-Packard garage or Mark Zuckerberg’s dorm room. It’s a story so compelling, people will want it to be true.
Elizabeth is more than a masterful storyteller. She writes the story. Every detail is meticulously chosen to build her narrative, captivate her audience, and distort reality. The black turtleneck, deep voice, college dropout — the parallels with Steve Jobs were no accident.
Related
Story
Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz on lessons learned, venture capital, and shutting down his own business
The very first time I met her, Elizabeth told my grandfather, George Shultz (who served in the Cabinet in the Nixon and Reagan administrations and became a member of the Theranos board), and then-Sen. Dianne Feinstein that Quest and LabCorp would eventually try to take her down. She was planting the seeds of a conspiracy years before she would need to lean on it. She also told us Theranos would never go public, preempting pressure from investors. She completely controlled the narrative from day one.
The Elizabeth I knew would openly talk about her decision to not have friends, to never date, to never have kids, all because she was devoted to Theranos. (This, of course, was another lie. She was dating Sunny Balwani, the COO and president of the company.) However, when motherhood made for a useful character reboot, she became one — twice. Her first child arrived just days before her trial was set to begin, and her second between her conviction and sentencing.
Before her sentencing, the
New York Times
wrote about how she had become “Liz,” the devoted mother and volunteer who had ditched the black turtleneck. The article even included carefully posed photographs of Elizabeth with her two children. I feel profound sadness for those kids. Most parents would try to shield their children from that type of attention, but Elizabeth put them front and center, using them the same way she used to use her black turtleneck. They were props to support the narrative she was writing.

data.title: Rolling Highway
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: "Rolling highways" or "rolling roads" refer to a form of combined transport in rail systems where road trucks are carried by trains, known as Ro-La trains. This concept is common in regions like Europe and North America, though technical challenges differ. In North America, the height allowance is sufficient for double-stack containers, while in Europe, due to smaller loading gauges, special wagons like "Modalohr," "CargoBeamer," and "Niederflurwagen" are used to transport trailers lower than the rail wagon wheels. Rolling highways are used extensively in transit routes through the Alps and across Europe. Austria, for example, operates rolling highways from Bavaria through Tyrol to Italy and Eastern Europe, while Switzerland uses them across the Gotthard and Lötschberg-Simplon routes. India introduced a similar Roll On Roll Off service on the Konkan Railway in 1999. These trains provide environmental benefits by reducing road traffic and are accompanied by accommodations for drivers.

主要讨论点：铁路与公路联运系统的现状及未来发展，包括技术创新、效率问题及不同运输方式的对比。

不同观点：
• **[Animats]**：在美国，集装箱运输已经成为主流，其他如公路铁路联运（piggyback）、平板车运输等方案已基本过时。双层集装箱火车的运力约为整辆卡车的4倍。

• **[Lammy]**：文章主要讨论货运，但Amtrak运营的乘客列车“汽车列车”（Auto Train）也值得关注。视频展示了列车卸载过程，突出了乘客运输的实际操作。

• **[theendisney]**：提到法国工业家的设计，设想了一种车辆与铁路混合的超长列车，卡车可以开到列车顶部并停放，利用重力前进。这是一种富有想象力的设计。

In rail transportation, a
rolling highway
or
rolling road
is a form of
combined transport
involving the conveying of
road trucks
by rail, referred to as Ro-La trains. The concept is a form of
piggyback transportation
.
The technical challenges to implement rolling highways vary from region to region.  In North America, the
loading gauge
is often high enough to accommodate
double stack containers
, so the height of a
semi-trailer
on a
flatcar
is no issue.  However, in Europe, except for purpose built lines such as the
Channel Tunnel
or the
Gotthard Base Tunnel
, the loading gauge height is much smaller, and it is necessary to transport the trailers with the tires about 30 cm (11.81 in) above the rails, so the trailers cannot be simply parked on the surface of a flat car above the
wagon wheels
or
bogies
.  Making the wagon wheels smaller limits the maximum speed, so many designs allow the trailer to be transported with its wheels lower than the rail wagon wheels.  An early approach in France was the
Kangourou wagon
[
1
]
with modified trailers. This technology did not survive, due to the market resistance to modified trailers. Today, three designs for these special wagons are in commercial service, "
Modalohr
", "
CargoBeamer
" and "Niederflurwagen"
[
2
]
[
3
]
[
4
]
.
During a rolling-highway journey, if the drivers accompany the trailer, they are accommodated in a
passenger car
or a
sleeping car
. At both ends of the rail link there are purpose-built terminals that allow the train to be easily loaded and unloaded.
Examples of rolling highways
[
edit
]
Rolling highways are mostly used for transit routes, e.g. through the
Alps
or from western to eastern Europe.
Austria

via

or to

. Traditionally, Austria is a transit country and therefore the rolling highway is of environmental importance. In 1999 the
Austrian Federal Railways
(ÖBB) carried 254,000 trucks, which equals 8,500,000 tonnes (8,400,000 long tons; 9,400,000 short tons) of load (including vehicle's weight) (158,989 trucks in 1993). The rolling highway trains in Austria are operated by Ökombi GmbH, a division of
Rail Cargo Austria
, the cargo division of ÖBB. There is a direct rolling highway between
Salzburg
and the harbour of
Trieste
, Italy, where the trucks arrive on
ferries
from
Turkey
. In those cases, drivers arrive by plane via

airport, to take over the trucks.

,

-

route. They are operated by RAlpin AG, headquartered in

.

has been made adequate to P\C 80

to conveying road trucks by train. Further upgrades are underway.

Two rolling highways are currently in operation in France, both using French Modalohr technology: the 175 km (109 mi)

, connecting the

region to Turin through the

43971442.article_summary: "Rolling highways" or "rolling roads" refer to a form of combined transport in rail systems where road trucks are carried by trains, known as Ro-La trains. This concept is common in regions like Europe and North America, though technical challenges differ. In North America, the height allowance is sufficient for double-stack containers, while in Europe, due to smaller loading gauges, special wagons like "Modalohr," "CargoBeamer," and "Niederflurwagen" are used to transport trailers lower than the rail wagon wheels. Rolling highways are used extensively in transit routes through the Alps and across Europe. Austria, for example, operates rolling highways from Bavaria through Tyrol to Italy and Eastern Europe, while Switzerland uses them across the Gotthard and Lötschberg-Simplon routes. India introduced a similar Roll On Roll Off service on the Konkan Railway in 1999. These trains provide environmental benefits by reducing road traffic and are accompanied by accommodations for drivers.

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Rust中构建一个无锁的固定大小数组`LockFreeArray<T, N>`，该数组使用原子操作和自由列表在多线程环境下存储和交换堆分配的值，而无需锁。文章详细讲解了如何使用`AtomicPtr`、`AtomicUsize`和`compare_exchange`等工具，以及内存顺序的重要性。无锁编程虽然速度快，但非常复杂且容易出错，需要开发者手动保证线程安全。文章还提供了具体代码实现，包括数组的初始化、尝试插入值和取出值的方法，并通过标记索引解决了ABA问题。总的来说，无锁编程类似于高风险的活动，虽然高效但需要极高的谨慎和技巧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于无锁数据结构的性能、实现细节、适用场景及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• gpderetta认为，无锁数组并不一定比有锁变体更快。无锁数组每次操作都需要执行一次CAS（Compare-And-Swap），这可能会成为性能瓶颈。相比之下，普通的互斥锁只需要两次CAS操作。如果互斥锁变体使用自由列表，性能差异也可以被解释。他强调无锁并不自动意味着更快，且基准测试需要谨慎对待。

• Animats分享了在Rust中进行无锁编程的实际案例，涉及在GPU和CPU之间同步状态。他指出无锁编程在特定场景下非常有用，例如无法直接读取某些状态时。

• MobiusHorizons对文中过度强调无锁数据结构的“危险性”和违规性表示不满，认为这种描述显得幼稚，并指出任何高度优化的结构都有其权衡和适用范围。

• 0x1ceb00da对文中将AtomicUsize描述为“被CPU时刻监视”的说法提出质疑，认为这是不准确的，因为重要的是原子加载/存储指令，而非AtomicUsize本身。

• tombert表示对Rust中的无锁结构感兴趣，但平常避免使用锁，而更倾向于使用Tokio channels进行并发处理，因为觉得锁难以推理。

• gmm1990提问自由列表相对于数组（如环形缓冲区）的优势，认为指针查找可能会增加延迟。

• zero0529喜欢文章的写作风格，但希望减少一些夸张的描述，认为这样会使文章更严谨。

• Fiahil提出了一种更进一步的无锁数组实现方式，通过不重新分配数组和不允许更新/删除已插入的值，但指出这种方法只适用于特定场景。

• rurban指出，即使使用无锁结构，如果IO是阻塞的，也无法实现真正的Rust并发安全。

• jillesvangurp提到Java的并发包提供了许多有用的无锁抽象和数据结构，并指出这是Java和JVM在构建中间件和数据处理框架方面受欢迎的原因之一。

补充讨论：
• fefe23引用了一句格言，暗示即使在高级语言中，程序员也可以写出像C语言一样的代码。

• jonco217提醒注意文中未详细讨论的ABA问题，这是一个在无锁编程中容易出错的地方。

• r3tr0解释了他在文章中使用幽默和类比的目的，是为了让难以理解的概念更加易懂和 memorable。

• lucraft提问关于Atomic操作的内部实现是否通过加锁实现。

• pjmlp评论文章中的截图风格受到了CDE的启发。

Lock-Free Rust: How to Build a Rollercoaster While Itâs on Fire
.
Posted on
2025-05-12
Author: Julian Goldstein
âEvery stitch in that flag was a commitment to thread safety without locks.
std::atomic
was the needle.â
â Betsy Ross, Federalist Papers, Draft 29 (suppressed), 1782
Buckle your seatbelts, grab a helmet, and say goodbye to your loved ones because over the next few minutes, I am going to teach you more about lock-free data structures in RustÂ than any human being should reasonably know without a psychiatric evaluation.
So sit down, shut up, and pretend you understand memory ordering, because thread safety is just a social construct and
Ordering::Relaxed
is just denial with extra steps.
TL;DR
Weâre buildingÂ
LockFreeArray<T, N>
, a fixed-size, lock-free array for storing heap-allocated values. It uses atomics and a freelist to insert and take values across threadsÂ
without locks
. Youâll learn:
HowÂ
AtomicPtr
,Â
AtomicUsize
, andÂ
compare_exchange
Â work.
Why memory ordering matters (and how to screw it up).
Where this kind of thing is useful (task slots, freelists, fixed-resource pools).
And why it's generally a terrible idea unless you're very desperate or very clever.
If you enjoy the read and want to see more content like this please check out our product
yeet
or our
sandbox
. Thank you.
Lock-Free: The Decathlon of Danger
Lock-free programming exists for the same reason people free solo climb cliffs without ropes: itâs fast, itâs elegant, and it absolutely will kill you if you do it wrong. Here at
yeet
, we have become masters in this. Specifically when it comes to building high-performance priority queues for real-time streaming of high volume events from BPF ring buffers.
WithÂ
Mutex<T>
Â andÂ
RwLock<T>
, you get warm, fuzzy guarantees â mutual exclusion, fairness, and the comfort of compile-time safety at the expense of speed. On the other hand, with lock-free, you get speed â but it's entirely on you to keep it safe. No waiting, no blocking, no help.
Itâs the difference between riding a rollercoaster and building one mid-air while itâs on fire â and youâre also the passenger.
Congratulations â if youâre still reading, youâve officially decided to ignore your therapist, ghost the borrow checker, and raw-dog concurrency.
Meet The Atomics
You donât need all of them â just the dangerous few:
AtomicPtr<T>
Think raw pointers, but in a shared haunted house. You can pass ownership between threads, but if you screw up, the ghost of undefined behavior will visit you at runtime.
AtomicUsize
Used for indexing and freelist linkage. Itâs a plain old number, except itâs watched 24 / 7 by the CPUâs race condition alarm.
Ordering::{Acquire, Release, AcqRel, Relaxed}
These decide
when
other threads can see your changes. Use the wrong one and your writes arrive out of order, like sending a cake before the ovenâs even preheated.
Thatâs it. Three tools. Infinite ways to wake up in a hospital wrapped in unsafe.
Lock-Free Arrays: Index at Your Own Risk
This isnât your friendly neighborhood
Vec<T>
. This is
Vec<Violence>
.
No resizing. No bounds checks. No cozy locks to hold your hand when the threads start racing. Just raw pointers, atomics, and the kind of confidence that comes from skimming half the docs, pounding gas station coffee, and whispering
âhow hard could it be?â
Weâll call it
LockFreeArray<T, N>
Think of it as a fixed-size concurrent slot buffer â useful for task pools, on-demand workers, or resource slots that canât afford a lock.
It has three methods:
new()
Initializes the array and sets up a freelist of available slots.
try_insert(value: T) -> Result<usize, T>
Tries to place a value in an empty slot. On success, returns the index. On failure, returns your value back, gently but firmly.
take(index: usize) -> Option<T>
Removes and returns the value
T
at the given
index
. If itâs already empty, returns
None
.

• 0x1ceb00da对文中将AtomicUsize描述为“被CPU时刻监视”的说法提出质疑，认为这是不准确的，因为重要的是原子加载/存储指令，而非AtomicUsize本身。

• tombert表示对Rust中的无锁结构感兴趣，但平常避免使用锁，而更倾向于使用Tokio channels进行并发处理，因为觉得锁难以推理。

• gmm1990提问自由列表相对于数组（如环形缓冲区）的优势，认为指针查找可能会增加延迟。

• zero0529喜欢文章的写作风格，但希望减少一些夸张的描述，认为这样会使文章更严谨。

• Fiahil提出了一种更进一步的无锁数组实现方式，通过不重新分配数组和不允许更新/删除已插入的值，但指出这种方法只适用于特定场景。

• rurban指出，即使使用无锁结构，如果IO是阻塞的，也无法实现真正的Rust并发安全。

• jillesvangurp提到Java的并发包提供了许多有用的无锁抽象和数据结构，并指出这是Java和JVM在构建中间件和数据处理框架方面受欢迎的原因之一。

补充讨论：
• fefe23引用了一句格言，暗示即使在高级语言中，程序员也可以写出像C语言一样的代码。

• jonco217提醒注意文中未详细讨论的ABA问题，这是一个在无锁编程中容易出错的地方。

• r3tr0解释了他在文章中使用幽默和类比的目的，是为了让难以理解的概念更加易懂和 memorable。

• lucraft提问关于Atomic操作的内部实现是否通过加锁实现。

• pjmlp评论文章中的截图风格受到了CDE的启发。

主要讨论点：数字取证（DFIR）工作中的心理影响及应对措施

不同观点：
• [0xbadc0de5] 认为在从事DFIR工作时，虽然没有接触到儿童性虐待材料（CSAM）或暴力内容，但目睹了许多诚实、努力工作的人被骗走一生积蓄的案例，特别是损失高达上百万美元的情况。这种经历让人感受到受害者的羞愧、绝望和失落，尽管不算创伤，但会长期留在记忆中。

• [bigfatkitten] 表示他们合作的机构在处理 traumatic 工作（如儿童保护）时有较好的措施，如轮换取证专家、提供支持系统和充足的休息时间。然而，像侦探和检察官等其他相关人员则往往没有得到足够的支持，被要求硬撑下去。

• [WaitWaitWha] 则直言因为无法承受此类工作的心理压力，已经放弃了数字取证的职业。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是不同机构在保护员工心理健康方面的措施是否充分。例如，[bigfatkitten] 提到一些机构有轮换和支持系统，而其他岗位如侦探和检察官则缺乏类似支持。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，不同的人对工作中的心理影响有不同的承受能力，[WaitWaitWha] 的例子表明有些人可能因为无法承受这些影响而选择离开这个行业。
• 评论中也隐含了对行业支持系统不平衡的批评，特别是在处理 traumatic 内容时，不同岗位的人员得到的支持不同。

data.title: Self Rewarding Self Improving: Autonomous LLM Improvement
data.author: tamassimond
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种通过自我评价实现自我改进的大语言模型方法。利用生成和验证解决方案之间的不对称性，模型无需参考答案即可自我评估并提供可靠的奖励信号，从而实现强化学习。实验表明，该方法在Countdown谜题和MIT Integration Bee问题上显著提升了性能，Qwen 2.5 7B模型相比基线提高了8%，并在积分任务上超越了GPT-4o。结合合成问题生成，模型能自主生成、解决和评估问题，形成完整的自我改进循环。该研究展示了LLM作为奖励信号的潜力，为缺乏训练数据或复杂评估的领域开辟了新的强化学习环境。

Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Self Rewarding Self Improving, by Toby Simonds and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We demonstrate that large language models can effectively self-improve through self-judging without requiring reference solutions, leveraging the inherent asymmetry between generating and verifying solutions. Our experiments on Countdown puzzles and MIT Integration Bee problems show that models can provide reliable reward signals without ground truth answers, enabling reinforcement learning in domains previously not possible. By implementing self-judging, we achieve significant performance gains maintaining alignment with formal verification. When combined with synthetic question generation, we establish a complete self-improvement loop where models generate practice problems, solve them, and evaluate their own performance-achieving an 8% improvement with Qwen 2.5 7B over baseline and surpassing GPT-4o performance on integration tasks. Our findings demonstrate that LLM judges can provide effective reward signals for training models, unlocking many reinforcement learning environments previously limited by the difficulty of creating programmatic rewards. This suggests a potential paradigm shift toward AI systems that continuously improve through self-directed learning rather than human-guided training, potentially accelerating progress in domains with scarce training data or complex evaluation requirements.

data.article_summary: HyprSqrl 是一个为自由职业者打造的开源银行平台，基于加密货币技术，提供多种金融服务。主要功能包括轻松创建发票、通过个人 IBAN 收款、无转换费用的全球借记卡支付、AI 自动优化闲置资金收益以及财务自动化。目前项目处于开发的早期阶段，已实现发票功能，后续将逐步推出 IBAN/USD 账户、收益优化和 AI 自动化等功能。技术上使用 Node.js 和 pnpm 进行开发，项目包含多个包，如基于 Next.js 的发票管理应用。HyprSqrl 旨在帮助用户更好地管理资金和自动化财务。

主要讨论点：围绕一个帮助主播通过加密货币和法币转换来规避税收的工具的可行性和实际用途

不同观点：
• [cluckindan的观点] 该工具类似于Revolut，旨在通过让在线赌场运营的流媒体网站在加密货币和法币之间转换支付，帮助有物质依赖的主播规避当地税收。cluckindan质疑这种操作的合法性，并暗示该工具可能被用来进行不透明的资金操作。

• [Mortiffer的观点] Mortiffer认为该工具在实际操作中存在困难。他指出，开设银行账户必须经过政府批准的资金管理账户，因此无法完全自我托管。此外，没有交易对手提供流动性，无法将加密货币转换为法定货币。Mortiffer对该工具能否如宣传的那样运作表示怀疑。

• [techplex的观点] techplex对该工具的实际功能和用途表示困惑，并请求更多信息。他认为该工具可能是用于在不同法币之间通过加密货币进行资金转移的工具，但对具体操作和优势尚不完全理解。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该工具的合法性和实际可行性。cluckindan和Mortiffer都对该工具是否能规避税收和其操作的可行性表示怀疑。
• techplex提出了对工具功能理解的困难，显示出对该工具的实际应用场景和用户需求存在不明确之处。
• Mortiffer特别指出了在加密货币和法币转换过程中需要交易对手提供流动性，这是该工具在实际操作中可能面临的一个重要问题。

通过这些观点可以看出，评论者们对于该工具的合法性、实际操作可行性以及用户对其功能的理解存在不同看法。

data.title: Show HN: Convert JSON Schema to SQL DDL
data.author: vjv
data.article_summary:
该文章介绍了`json-schema-to-sql`库，它能将JSON schema转换为SQL DDL（创建表）语句。该库支持将JSON Schema的特性映射到关系数据库，例如类型、格式、必填项、枚举、默认值和描述等。它通过扩展JSON Schema规范（如`x-primaryKey`）来实现数据库特定功能，如主键设置，并计划未来支持`x-onDelete`和`x-onUpdate`。

该库完全使用TypeScript编写，支持PostgreSQL和MySQL数据库方言。它能处理嵌套结构，将其规范化为单独的表，并通过外键引用父表。嵌套对象和对象数组会分别处理为1:1和1:N的关系，而字面量数组则创建单列表。

使用方法简单，通过`npm install json-schema-to-sql`安装，并使用`generateSQLFromJSONSchema`函数生成SQL语句。

Features
JSON Schema Compatible
The library aims to map features of the JSON Schema spec as closely as possible to their logical counterpart in
relational databases.
A few examples:
JSON Schema Feature
Database Feature
type
+
format
Type of the column
required
Non nullable columns
enum
CHECK constraint for the possible values
default
Default value of the column
description
Column comment
JSON Schema Extensions
Where a logical mapping is not possible, the library extends the JSON Schema spec using
the
x-
syntax
For example:
JSON Schema Feature
Database Feature
x-primaryKey
Sets primary keys in the table
In the future, things like
x-onDelete
and
x-onUpdate
will be added to support cascades.
Unmapped Features
JSON Schema features, which are not yet implemented or will never be implemented are just ignored by the converter.
Fully Typed
All the internals use TypeScript.
Supported Dialects
Currently, it supports
PostgreSQL
and
MySQL
by passing
pg
and
mysql
respectively to the function. Default is
pg
.
Every example in this README will be using PostgreSQL.
Nested Structures
Nested structures are normalized into tables, which reference their parent table by a dynamically generated
foreign key
.

In this schema:
settings
is a nested object

is a nested array of strings
The library will take care of the nesting by mapping each of the nested structures into a table. This table will have

Arrays of Objects

1:N (One-to-Many)

A table with a single column called

with the type of the items will be created. This relationship is considered
1:N (One-to-Many)

43999439.article_summary:
该文章介绍了`json-schema-to-sql`库，它能将JSON schema转换为SQL DDL（创建表）语句。该库支持将JSON Schema的特性映射到关系数据库，例如类型、格式、必填项、枚举、默认值和描述等。它通过扩展JSON Schema规范（如`x-primaryKey`）来实现数据库特定功能，如主键设置，并计划未来支持`x-onDelete`和`x-onUpdate`。

该库完全使用TypeScript编写，支持PostgreSQL和MySQL数据库方言。它能处理嵌套结构，将其规范化为单独的表，并通过外键引用父表。嵌套对象和对象数组会分别处理为1:1和1:N的关系，而字面量数组则创建单列表。

使用方法简单，通过`npm install json-schema-to-sql`安装，并使用`generateSQLFromJSONSchema`函数生成SQL语句。

data.title: Why bad philosophy is stopping progress in physics
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了当今物理学界过于专注于寻找超越现有理论（如标准模型、广义相对论和量子理论）的物理学，而实验结果却一再证实旧有理论的有效性。作者指出，像希格斯玻色子的发现、引力波的探测以及量子纠缠的验证等都只是证实了数十年前的理论，而非支持新的推测性理论。作者认为，这种对“超越”理论的执着源于对卡尔·波普尔和托马斯·库恩哲学思想的误读，导致物理学家忽略了过去知识的价值，并一味追求全新的理论。这种态度阻碍了物理学的进步，呼吁同行应更加谦虚和审慎地对待理论研究。

44001212.article_content:
Why bad philosophy is stopping progress in physics
Download PDF
Twitter
Facebook
Email
You have full access to this article via your institution.
Download PDF
Physicists have developed an obsession for finding hints of physics ‘beyond’ what we already know.
Credit: Roger Ressmeyer/Corbis/VCG via Getty
Nature seems to have played us for a fool in the past few decades. Much theoretical research in fundamental physics during this time has focused on the search ‘beyond’ our best theories: beyond the standard model of particle physics, beyond the general theory of relativity, beyond quantum theory. But an epochal sequence of experimental results has proved many such speculations unfounded, and confirmed physics that I learnt at school half a century ago. I think physicists are failing to heed the lessons — and that, in turn, is hindering progress in physics.
Take the
2012 discovery of the Higgs boson
using the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN, Europe’s particle-physics laboratory near Geneva, Switzerland. Peter Higgs and François Englert, two of the theorists who had established the underlying theory almost 50 years earlier,
shared the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics
for this feat. The Higgs boson was the last particle of the standard model of particle physics to be discovered, and spectacularly confirmed that model, rather than the dozens of theories beyond it. Meanwhile, the apparent absence of evidence for ‘supersymmetric’ particles in LHC data has disappointed a generation of theoretical physicists who had bet on such particles existing, motivated by speculative theories, including string theory.
The expanding Universe — do ongoing tensions leave room for new physics?
Or take the
first direct detection of gravitational waves
in 2015. This was a spectacular confirmation of Albert Einstein’s century-old theory of gravity, general relativity. The
2017 physics Nobel
went to three physicists who had made decisive theoretical and experimental contributions to the discovery.
That same year, the near-simultaneous
detection of gravitational and electromagnetic signals
from the fusion of two neutron stars (the event GW170817) improved scientists’ knowledge of the ratio between the speeds of gravitational and electromagnetic waves (which general relativity implies should be the same) by some 14 orders of magnitude. In one fell swoop, this excluded a huge domain of theories beyond general relativity. In a similar vein, the
2020 Nobel Prize in Physics
was awarded for work showing that the existence and phenomenology of black holes were in complete agreement with general relativity.
And, finally, take the
2022 physics Nobel
, awarded for experiments performed over decades that verified phenomena such as quantum entanglement over great distances, falsifying speculation about theories beyond quantum mechanics. These results are often presented as surprising, but in fact they just confirmed what I was taught in school.
And yet, for decades, every new data point in particle physics or astronomy that seemed to be in some slight tension with established ideas has been announced as a hint of physics ‘beyond’ current theories. Large communities of physicists have used such hints as a springboard for speculations, producing a forest of papers in the process. But these new data have always turned out to be explicable by established physics, by statistical fluctuations — or even by experimental error.
You might think that this repeated ‘no’ to wild speculations beyond our best theories would encourage a certain humility in our methodological attitude. Yet I see little evidence for that among many of my fellow theorists, who remain intent on pursuing the next big theory ‘beyond’ those we have today. Why?
Bad digestion
My hunch is that it is at least partly because physicists are bad philosophers. Scientists’ opinions, whether they realize it or not (and whether they like it or not), are imbued with philosophy. And many of my colleagues — especially those who argue that philosophy is irrelevant — have an idea of what science should do that originates in badly digested versions of the work of two twentieth-century philosophers: Karl Popper and Thomas Kuhn.
From Kuhn comes the idea that new scientific theories are not grounded in previous ones: progress instead comes about through ‘paradigm shifts’, the scientific equivalents of revolutions. Popper, meanwhile, supplies the notion that a theory is scientific only if it is ‘falsifiable’: if it can be proved wrong by empirical evidence. Superficial readings of Popper and Kuhn, I think, have encouraged several assumptions that have misled a good deal of research: one, that past knowledge is not a good guide for the future and that new theories must be fished from the sky; and two, that all theories that have not yet been falsified should be considered equally plausible and in equal need of being tested.

data.title: You Don't Have a Right to a Bank Account
data.author: like_any_other
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：银行业务与金融监管的合法性和道德性，特别是关于银行业选择客户的权利与金融监管的关系。

不同观点：
• **elmerfud的观点**：认为个人没有绝对的“银行权利”，即任何人不能强制银行必须为某人提供服务。然而，elmerfud对银行和金融机构选择性接受现金或拒绝某些客户表示怀疑，暗示这可能是政府用来控制和追踪个人的手段。该评论表达了对金融监管和隐私的担忧。

• **techpineapple的观点**：认为因政治、道德或伦理观点而拒绝提供银行服务是一个复杂的问题。特别是讨论了加密货币公司与银行之间的关系，提出了“什么是银行”的哲学问题。techpineapple提到银行需要与大型金融机构对接，同时指出银行不应被迫向高风险客户提供贷款，但这种风险评估应该是基于客观标准。此外，techpineapple质疑银行对现金业务的担忧，尤其是当这些业务可能涉及无法追踪来源的大额资金时，如涉及加密货币或潜在的非法活动（如毒品交易）。

• **like_any_other的观点**：引用具体资料，指出媒体和文章在描述“Operation Choke Point”时存在误导性。like_any_other强调，尽管文章表面上仅描述法律，但忽略了该计划实际针对的合法企业范围广泛，包括枪支相关业务、弹药销售、快速致富计划、在线赌博等。同时提到政府明确禁止银行歧视非法移民，认为媒体报道存在“遗漏谎言”的问题。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：在于银行是否有权基于风险或其他考量拒绝某些客户或业务，以及政府金融监管计划（如Operation Choke Point）的合法性与透明度。elmerfud和techpineapple对银行选择性服务的担忧与like_any_other对监管计划实际执行中的信息披露问题形成对比，反映出公众对金融监管和隐私保护的不同看法。

• **重要论据和例子**：
  - elmerfud对金融隐私和政府监控的怀疑。
  - techpineapple提出的银行与加密货币公司之间的潜在风险问题。
  - like_any_other引用的具体例子和参考资料，揭示媒体在报道金融监管计划时的信息遗漏和误导性描述。

data.title: Show HN: HelixDB – Open-source vector-graph database for AI applications (Rust)
data.author: GeorgeCurtis
data.article_summary: HelixDB 是一个开源的图-向量数据库，使用Rust开发，专为RAG（检索增强生成）和AI应用设计。它基于LMDB存储引擎，具有高性能和高效性，速度比Neo4j快1000倍，比TigerGraph快100倍，支持图和向量数据类型，具备ACID特性，确保数据完整性。HelixDB提供CLI工具，便于数据库的安装、初始化、查询和部署，并支持TypeScript和Python SDK进行开发。未来计划包括扩展向量数据类型能力、增强查询语言、实施测试套件和开发自有存储引擎及网络协议。该项目遵循AGPL-3.0许可证，并提供商业支持选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕新发布的Helixdb项目的技术设计、应用场景及与其他数据库系统的对比，社区进行了多方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• **赞赏与支持**：
  - [rohanrao123] 对项目的发布表示祝贺，并表示他们引用的论文能为该项目提供帮助，愿意提供进一步支持。

• **硬件需求与性能考虑**：
  - [srameshc] 对项目在图形数据库与向量数据库结合的硬件需求方面表示关注，担心RAM和计算资源的消耗问题。

• **浏览器与WASM支持**：
  - [hbcondo714] 询问项目是否能在浏览器中通过WASM运行，以便在客户端进行查询，满足隐私和合规需求。

• **写入机制与优化**：

HelixDB
: an open-source graph-vector database written in Rust built for RAG and AI applications.
Homepage
|
Docs
|
Discord
|
X
HelixDB is a high-performance graph-vector database  designed with a focus on developer experience and performance. Built in Rust and powered by LMDB as its storage engine, it combines the reliability of a proven storage layer with modern features tailored for AI and vector-based applications.
We are currently using LMDB via Heed3, a rust wrapper built by the amazing team over at
Meilisearch
.
Key Features
Fast & Efficient
: Built for performance we're currently 1000x faster than Neo4j, 100x faster than TigerGraph and on par with Qdrant for vectors.
RAG-First
: Native support for graph and vector data types, making it ideal for RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) and AI applications
Graph-Vector
: Easiest database for storing relationships between nodes, vectors, or nodes AND vectors.
Reliable Storage
: Powered by LMDB (Lightning Memory-Mapped Database) for robust and efficient data persistence
ACID Compliant
: Ensures data integrity and consistency

Our current focus areas include:
Expanding vector data type capabilities for RAG applications

In-house network protocol & serdes libraries (similar to protobufs/gRPC)

data.title: Bringing 3D shoppable products online with generative AI
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary:
谷歌实验室的最新AI技术利用生成式AI将2D产品图像转化为沉浸式3D体验。传统在线购物难以复制实体店中的直观感受，而现有的3D可视化工具对企业来说成本高且耗时。为此，谷歌开发了新的生成式AI技术，仅需三张产品图片即可生成高质量的3D产品视图。

初期技术（2022年）使用神经辐射场（NeRF）从五张以上的图片生成360°旋转视图，但存在噪声和视角稀疏的问题。2023年，谷歌引入第二代技术，采用视图条件扩散模型（view-conditioned diffusion model），通过分数蒸馏采样（SDS）优化3D模型，成功解决了视角有限的问题，并实现了鞋类产品的广泛应用。

最新技术（第三代）基于谷歌先进的视频生成模型Veo，能够生成复杂的灯光、材质和几何交互视频，进一步提升了3D视图的质量和真实感，已在谷歌购物中应用于多种产品类别。

• [dagmx] 批评将此技术应用于电子商务领域的做法，指出大多数产品已有CAD模型，使用传统工具（如mesher和decimation）可以获得更好且无“幻觉”问题的结果。此外，对虚假广告和责任问题表示担忧，认为这是市场营销对研发的误用。
• [Huxley1] 支持该技术，认为它能为没有专业摄影资源的卖家提供帮助，尤其是处理反射和半透明物体方面，可能会是一个重大突破。对小卖家来说可能是一个竞争优势。
• [allears] 以讽刺的语气评论，暗示顶尖人才正在将精力浪费在提升购物体验这样的领域上。

- 其他评论者（如[Huxley1]）则看好该技术在特定场景（如小卖家）中的应用潜力。
- [ivanjermakov] 和 [allears] 对该技术是否必要和价值提出质疑，尤其是与现有解决方案的对比。

43974344.article_content:
Bringing 3D shoppable products online with generative AI
May 12, 2025
Steve Seitz, Distinguished Scientist, Google Labs
Discover how our latest AI models transform 2D product images into immersive 3D experiences for online shoppers.
Every day, billions of people shop online, hoping to replicate the best parts of in-store shopping. Seeing something that catches your eye, picking it up and inspecting it for yourself can be a key part of how we connect with products. But capturing the intuitive, hands-on nature of the store experience is nuanced and can be challenging to replicate on a screen. We know that technology can help bridge the gap, bringing key details to your fingertips with a quick scroll. But these online tools can be costly and time consuming for businesses to create at scale.
To address this, we developed new generative AI techniques to create high quality and shoppable 3D product visualizations from as few as three product images. Today, we're excited to share the latest advancement, powered by Google’s state-of-the-art video generation model,
Veo
. This technology is already enabling the generation of interactive 3D views for a wide range of product categories on Google Shopping
play silent looping video
pause silent looping video
Examples of 3D product visualizations generated from photos.
First generation: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs)
In 2022, researchers from across Google came together to develop technologies to make product visualization more immersive. The initial efforts focused on using
Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)
to learn a 3D representation of products to render novel views (i.e., novel view synthesis), like 360° spins, from five or more images of the product. This required solving many sub-problems, including selecting the most informative images, removing unwanted backgrounds, predicting 3D priors, estimating camera positions from a sparse set of object-centric images, and optimizing a 3D representation of the product.
That same year, we
announced
this breakthrough and launched the first milestone, interactive 360° visualizations of shoes on Google Search. While this technology was promising, it suffered from noisy input signals (e.g., inaccurate camera poses) and ambiguity from sparse input views. This challenge became apparent when attempting to reconstruct sandals and heels, whose thin structures and more complex geometry was tricky to reconstruct from just a handful of images.
This led us to wonder: could the recent advancements in generative diffusion models help us improve the learned 3D representation?
Our first-generation approach used neural radiance fields (
NeRF
) to render novel views, combining several 3D techniques like
NOCS
for XYZ prediction,
CamP
for camera optimization, and
Zip-NeRF
for state-of-the-art novel view synthesis from a sparse set of views.
Second generation: Scaling with a view-conditioned diffusion prior
In 2023, we introduced a second-generation approach which used a view-conditioned diffusion prior to address the limitations of the first approach. Being
view-conditioned
means that you can give it an image of the top of a shoe and ask the model
“what does the front of this shoe look like?”
In this way, we can use the
view-conditioned diffusion model
to help predict what the shoe looks like from any viewpoint, even if we only have photos of limited viewpoints.
In practice, we employ a variant of
score distillation sampling
(SDS), first proposed in
DreamFusion
. During training, we render the 3D model from a random camera view. We then use the view-conditioned diffusion model and the available posed images to generate a target from the same camera view. Finally, we calculate a score by comparing the rendered image and the generated target. This score directly informs the optimization process, refining the 3D model's parameters and enhancing its quality and realism.
This second-generation approach led to significant scaling advantages enabling us to generate 3D representations for many of the shoes viewed daily on Google Shopping. Today, you can find interactive 360° visualizations for sandals, heels, boots, and other footwear categories when you shop on Google, the majority of which are created by this technology!
The second-generation approach used a view-conditioned diffusion model based on the
TryOn
architecture. The diffusion model acts as a learned prior using score distillation sampling proposed in
DreamFusion
to improve the quality and fidelity of novel views.
Third generation: Generalizing with Veo
Our latest breakthrough builds on
Veo
, Google's state-of-the-art video generation. A key strength of Veo is its ability to generate videos that capture complex interactions between light, material, texture, and geometry. Its powerful diffusion-based architecture and its ability to be finetuned on a variety of multi-modal tasks enable it to excel at novel view synthesis.
To finetune Veo to transform product images into a consistent 360° video, we

data.article_summary: 墨西哥拥有68种官方认可的土著语言，近700万人使用，包括玛雅语和纳瓦特尔语。然而，由于城市化、全球化以及西班牙语和英语的主导地位，许多土著语言正面临消亡的威胁。为保护这一丰富的语言遗产，墨西哥政府启动了土著语言课程和双语课程的计划。在尤卡坦州，约35,000名学生可以选择学习尤卡坦玛雅语。墨西哥城将有78所学校开设纳瓦特尔语课程。尽管资源有限和方言差异等挑战依然存在，学生和社区的热情日益增长，显示出土著语言在墨西哥身份认同中的持久价值。同时，土著语言还面临着历史遗留的歧视问题，保护这些语言不仅是保存词汇，更是维护土著人民的尊严和身份。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：纳瓦特语及其他土著语言在现代社会中的地位与复兴努力

不同观点：
• [jf] 认为纳瓦特语的复兴与墨西哥的“印第根主义运动”有关，并指出纳瓦特词汇对墨西哥西班牙语及英语的影响。他通过家族名字的例子，展现个人与这段历史的联系，并对纳瓦特语在现代语言中的影响表示兴趣。
• [dhosek] 指出“玛雅语言”这一术语具有误导性，因为玛雅实际上有多种不同的语言。他还强调墨西哥是世界上语言最多样的国家之一，并批评人们常常将土著文化扁平化，尤其是将玛雅文化视为单一的、已消亡的文化，而实际上它是多样且充满活力的。
• [eschulz] 分享了在墨西哥城一家养老院遇到的年轻护理员主要讲 Zapotec 语言的经历，表明在墨西哥仍有许多人在使用土著语言。
• [stackedinserter] 持较为悲观的观点，认为像纳瓦特语这样的土著语言难以复兴，最终会被主要语言如西班牙语、英语等吸收。他指出，除非土著语言在年轻一代中重新流行，否则这些语言将逐渐消失，并认为社会的城市化趋势使得语言复兴变得不现实。
• [neilshev] 讨论了爱尔兰复兴爱尔兰语的失败案例，认为一旦语言的使用者数量低于某个临界值，就很难再复兴。他还提到，双语社会常见，但土著语言往往被视为“无用”或“古老”的，除非通过强制手段（如希伯来语的复兴），否则复兴非常困难。
• [thunder-blue-3] 认为讨论土著语言复兴是次要的，墨西哥有更紧迫的社会问题（如暴力犯罪和基本人权问题）需要解决，表明语言问题在这些问题面前显得不重要。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是土著语言是否能够在现代社会中复兴。乐观者如 [jf] 认为复兴是有可能的，而悲观者如 [stackedinserter] 和 [neilshev] 则认为复兴难度极大。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是土著文化的多样性及其被忽视的问题，[dhosek] 强调了不应将土著文化视为单一的整体。
• 社会问题与语言复兴的关系也被提及，[thunder-blue-3] 认为应首先解决基本人权问题，再考虑语言复兴。

43974461.article_content:
Mexico is home to 68 officially recognized Indigenous languages, spoken by nearly 7 million people, including Mayan and Náhuatl. Yet, despite their historical significance, many of these languages are in decline. Urbanization, globalization, and the dominance of Spanish and English are slowly but surely pushing them to the brink.
To preserve Mexico’s rich linguistic heritage, Mexican authorities have kick-started an initiative to offer Indigenous language classes, and, in some cases, fully bilingual curriculums.
In Yucatán, efforts to teach the Maya language in schools are gaining momentum as 35,000 students from 75 municipalities now
have the option to study Yucatec-Maya
, beginning as early as grade school.
Náhuatl and Mayan Language Renaissance
The broader initiative includes efforts to preserve and revitalize Indigenous culture by recognizing the importance of Mexico’s Prehispanic heritage and how it connects with its cultural and historical significance.
The Mexican government’s commitment to this cause is reflected in the General Law of Linguistic Rights of Indigenous Peoples, which recognizes Indigenous languages as having equal validity with Spanish.
In Mexico City,
78 schools
will begin offering Náhuatl language classes in the next few weeks. Although Náhuatl is the most widely spoken Indigenous language on the entire American continent, it shows signs of quickly vanishing, especially among younger generations.
Classical age Maya stelae of Yaxilan depict two nobles in conversation. Photo: Carlos Rosado van der Gracht / Yucatán Magazine
“Náhuatl has since time immemorial been the language of the people of the valley of Mexico, but it’s not just a tongue of the past. It must be preserved as a living language into the future as part of our nation’s heritage,” said Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada.
Across the country, similar initiatives are underway to promote the use of Indigenous languages like Zapotec and Mixtec, which have been spoken for centuries but now face the threat of extinction.
These classes are designed to teach vocabulary and grammar and immerse students in the cultural context of the languages. Through storytelling, traditional songs, and rituals, students gain a deeper understanding of the worldviews embedded in these ancient tongues.
In Yucatán, adult students can enroll in
Mayan language
classes at
INDEMAYA
, the Autonomous University of Yucatán, the Municipal Mayan Language Academy “Itzamná,” as well as at the UNAM’s
Cephcis language center
.
Growing Enthusiasm  for Indigenous languages
While challenges such as limited resources and varying dialects persist, the growing enthusiasm among students and communities signals a promising future for Indigenous languages, ensuring they remain an enduring part of Mexico’s identity.
It is important to keep in mind that indigenous languages in Mexico, are often met with discrimination. This prejudice stems from a complex web of historical, social, and economic factors that continue to marginalize indigenous communities.
The roots of this discrimination trace back to the Spanish colonization of Mexico. Spanish colonizers imposed their language and culture, creating a hierarchy where indigenous languages were deemed inferior. This legacy of cultural erasure persists today, as Spanish remains the dominant language in education, media, and government, while indigenous languages are often excluded from these spaces.
Social and racial prejudices further compound the issue. Indigenous people, who are frequently among the poorest in Mexico, face stereotypes that label their languages and cultures as “backward” or “outdated.” Speaking an indigenous language can lead to discrimination in urban areas, where Spanish is seen as the language of opportunity and modernity.
The fight for indigenous languages in Mexico is not just about preserving words; it’s about reclaiming identity, dignity, and a place in a society that has long marginalized its native peoples. By embracing linguistic diversity, Mexico can move closer to a future where all its voices are heard and valued.
Carlos Rosado van der Gracht
Senior Editor Carlos Rosado van der Gracht is a Mexican expedition/Canadian photographer, adventure leader, and PhD candidate. Born in Mérida, Carlos holds multimedia, philosophy, and translation degrees from universities in Mexico, Canada and Norway.

data.title: Comma 3X: Initial Impressions
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Comma 3X设备的功能、合法性、安全性以及对驾驶 vertigo 患者的适用性。

不同观点：
• Vasco 和 Havoc 认为，如果一个人患有严重的眩晕症，在驾驶过程中可能无法控制车辆直线行驶或应对紧急情况，那么他们就不应该驾驶。Vasco 提到不同地区对驾驶健康条件的规定不同，而 Havoc 则强烈反对让可能突然失去控制能力的司机上路，认为这是对他人的生命构成威胁。

• Msbcuck 支持 Comma 3X，认为它在交通和高速驾驶中表现良好，尤其是在车辆原装的驾驶辅助系统无法使用时。然而，他们也提到新模型的改进未达预期，并对某些技术问题表示担忧。

• Shellfishgene 对在美国可以安装第三方硬件和软件来控制车辆的合法性表示惊讶，因为他们所在地区对改装件有严格的规定。

• Optimusprinceps 对 Comma 3X 的功能感到困惑，不理解其与普通 dashcam 的区别，并对产品的宣传和说明提出质疑。

• Nancyminusone 对 Comma 3X 的广告和公开讨论中提及的健康问题表示不满，并质疑产品在驾驶辅助方面的改进承诺，同时指出公开承认某些健康问题可能会影响驾照资格。

• Theparanoid 分享了个人使用 Comma 3X 的经验，认为它类似于特斯拉的自动驾驶系统，在高速公路上表现出色，但在城市街道上不理想。

• Krosaen 对使用 Comma 3X 的法律责任问题表示担忧，认为产品制造商不承担任何责任会造成不良激励，并希望有更多安全保障。

• Mtlynch 表达了对 AI 驾驶控制的不安，并希望有一种系统能被动监控驾驶并提供安全反馈，帮助改进驾驶行为。

• Farmdve 对 Comma 3X 的某些功能感兴趣，但不愿意为了实现这些功能而修改车辆的固件，担心操作不当可能带来的风险。

补充讨论：
• Dep_b 和 Coolcase 的评论与主要讨论主题无直接关系，前者是幽默评论，后者是关于健康建议。
• 争议的焦点在于 Comma 3X 是否能安全地用于患有严重健康问题的驾驶者，以及在公共道路上使用此类设备的合法性和道德性。

data.title: "Goodwill", key member of the SoCal Python Community has passed away
data.author: rdegges
data.article_summary: 本文是悼念Southern California Python社区的组织者Michael Ryabushkin（网名goodwill）的悼文。他于2025年5月初去世，对社区的影响深远。Michael多年来组织了多次活动和会议，如SoCal Python和PyBeach，还为多个开源项目和社区做出贡献。他以无私的帮助和善意著称，总是乐于介绍人们互相认识，创造职业机会和友谊。他鼓励他人回馈社区，并以导师和朋友的身份支持许多人，包括帮助别人转行技术领域。他的幽默、善良和无私让很多人怀念。Michael的离去是社区的重大损失，他将被深深怀念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Michael的缅怀与赞扬，以及他在Python开发者社区中的贡献

不同观点：
• [rdegges] 对是否发布纪念消息存在犹豫，但最终决定分享。他强调Michael是一个善良的人，对洛杉矶Python开发者社区的成长贡献卓著。他还提到Michael是一个优秀的工程师和黑客，并邀请认识Michael的人在他的纪念页面上分享经历。

• [cafard] 简单直接地表达了对Michael的赞赏，称他为一个杰出的人，但没有提供具体细节。

• [john-tells-all] 详细描述了Michael对社区的无私奉献，包括他如何不知疲倦地帮助人们建立联系，确保大家都能享受社区活动。他还提到Michael积极寻找并鼓励像他这样的演讲者和教师。John表示很乐意通过讲述Michael的故事来缅怀他。

补充讨论：
• Michael的个人品质和对社区的贡献是大家讨论的重点，特别是他帮助连接社区成员和鼓励新人参与的活动。
• 不同的评论者通过各自的视角分享了对Michael的回忆和感激，展现了Michael的多方面影响。
• 争议方面，评论中没有明显的对立观点或争议，所有评论者都一致对Michael表达了高度的赞扬和怀念。

44001734.article_content:
In Memoriam: Michael
In early May of 2025, the long-standing SoCal Python organizer Michael Ryabushkin—known to many as goodwill—passed away.
As possibly the person most responsible for years of thriving of the group and its surrounding community, he had an impact on many of us, both professionally and personally. In light of that, this page is a collection of
in memoriam
messages submitted through
this form
. If you would like to share your memories of Michael, please do the same.
Michael and I met in 2017, when I started attending SoCal Python meetups. Pretty soon he brought me under his wing as a co-organizer, and over the ensuing years we and others organized many SoCal Python events together, and even the inaugural PyBeach conference. His helpfulness and influence on everything he contributed to are hard to overstate. He was engaged in many other communities as well, and it’s no secret or surprise that many people active in them knew him and appreciated his work.
Somewhere in there Michael and I became friends as well. I don’t know if he knew how to operate in any other way, and I think that line was rather blurred for him in general, since he always sought ways to help other people. The number of times I’ve witnessed him introduce two people to each other is beyond any count, and that’s basically what he was about: making connections. These connections lead to job opportunities, friendships, and who knows what else.
The Southern California Python community has lost one of its major champions, and he will be greatly missed. Rest in peace, goodwill.
— Nik Kantar, May 2025
I met Michael at a PyLadies event in 2011.  He'd offered his company's office space for some of the workshops and hackathons that PyLadies was running at the time. That was the first of many events that we would organize together, over more than a decade. When SoCal Python needed more organizers in 2013, Michael volunteered countless hours to organize monthly meetups where folks from LA and Orange Counties could gather to share knowledge, stories, and skills with each other. On top of that, Michael wrangled his employer into sponsoring numerous events and open source projects, including Plone and Pyramid, Nix, PyCon US, the SoCal Linux Expo, and so many more.  His work helped sustain an active commmunity of hundreds of Python and open source enthusiasts.
Michael always kept a keen eye out for those in need of help. He would never hesitate to give generously of his time and resources.  Michael once told me "a stranger is just a friend you haven't met yet", and he had many friends, whether they knew it or not!  At the time I met Michael, I was freelancing part-time as a web developer to make ends meet. Michael convinced me to change careers, assuring me against my many doubts that I could be successful as a full-time software developer, even opening up a junior developer role at his company to hire me into my first professional job in tech. Without exaggeration, Michael forever changed the course of my life, as he changed the lives of many others.
Michael loved terrible jokes and puns, often repeating his favorites to the point where everyone got sick of them (I suspect this had to be one more reason why he loved meeting new people, for whom these jokes would be fresh material again!). At tech conferences, he made his presence known almost everywhere, as he sought out new people to get to know better, and talked with old friends and new, sometimes through the night - sleep was an after-thought during such weeks.
The SoCal Python community will not be the same without Michael. He was a true leader, a great mentor, and a friend without peer. I will miss him terribly.
— Esther, May 2025
For a few years, Michael was my manager. For many more years, he was also my mentor and friend. He saw his purpose in challenging people and breaking them out of their boxes. He loved to teach, and was always generous with his time. And he encouraged me to give back by helping, advising, and mentoring others. I can't believe Michael is not with us anymore. data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI 收购 WindSurf 及其对编码专用 AI 模型的影响

不同观点：
• **resters 的观点**：
   - OpenAI 收购 WindSurf 是基于对其模型的尽职调查和潜在价值的评估。
   - WindSurf 可能通过用户数据帮助训练编码专用 AI 模型，从而为 OpenAI 带来六个月的领先优势，这可能值 30 亿美元。
   - 即使 WindSurf 的模型在编码方面并非最优，但在某些关键领域的卓越表现足以证明对其方法论的大量投资是合理的。
   - 当前的顶级模型在处理特定框架、编程语言版本等方面仍有改进空间，尤其是在支持较 obscure 的语言和库版本方面。

• **antirez 的观点**：
   - 收购可能导致用户被迫使用较弱的模型，而不是最好的可用模型。
   - "AI inside the editor" 模式限制了开发者的自由，使设计交互过于关注代码而非设计本身。
   - 不能同时订阅多个顶级 LLM 并根据需要选择使用，这降低了灵活性。

• **bluelightning2k 的观点**：
   - ** cynical 看法**：将自己描述为全栈 AI IDE 公司听起来很有投资吸引力，可能要求更高的估值。
   - ** optimistic 看法**：针对特定用例（不完整代码片段和特定数据模型）进行微调应是有效的，具备合理的技能和经验。
   - ** bonus 看法**：可能意味着他们正在通过大规模收集用户数据进行训练。

• **firejake308 的观点**：
   - 困惑于 WindSurf 为什么在即将被 OpenAI 收购的情况下还要开发自己的前沿模型，可能是在收购前已经进行的工作。

• **blixt 的观点**：
   - WindSurf 的编辑器提供了有价值的洞察，帮助构建新的数据模型和训练方法，这对于创建全自动软件工程师非常有价值。
   - 相比之下，其他基础模型提供商可能只能依赖二手数据进行长周期工程工作的模拟。

• **dyl000 的观点**：
   - OpenAI 拥有大量优质数据，训练自己的模型是必然的，且 Claude API 调用可能影响其盈利能力。
   - 提到一个开源替代方案，但指出该方案存在问题。

• **aquir 的观点**：
   - 由于开发工作需要特定的 VSCode 扩展，只能选择 VSCode+Copilot 或 Cursor，限制了选择。

• **infecto 的观点**：
   - 请求提供 arm Linux 版本的构建。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及模型训练数据的获取、处理和价值，尤其是用户数据的重要性。
- 不同用户对使用特定编辑器扩展的依赖性和选择受限的问题。
- 对开源替代方案的提及和对不同平台支持的需求（如 arm Linux 构建）。
- 争议的焦点在于收购后的模型选择和用户体验的自由度，以及开源与专有解决方案的对比。
